ch-berres.name: C.H. Berres
ch-berres.line: A family estate in Ürzig on the Middle Mosel, making bright, slate-grown Riesling.
ch-berres.tell: Berres is a family estate in Ürzig on the Mosel. The Old Vines Riesling is crisp and lightly fruity, with the stony edge slate soil gives, and it is a friendly first white for a guest who thinks Riesling is always sweet.

pazo-das-bruxas.name: Pazo das Bruxas
pazo-das-bruxas.line: An Albariño from Rías Baixas on the Atlantic coast of Galicia, made by the Torres family.
pazo-das-bruxas.tell: Pazo das Bruxas is Albariño from Rías Baixas, the rainy, sea-facing corner of northwest Spain. It is fresh, citrusy and a little saline, built for seafood, so it sits happily beside oysters, crab and anything with lemon.

gainey.name: Gainey Vineyard
gainey.region: Santa Ynez Valley and Sta. Rita Hills, California
gainey.line: A family estate in Santa Barbara County, farming cool Sta. Rita Hills fruit for Chardonnay and Pinot Noir.
gainey.tell: Gainey is a family winery in Santa Barbara County. Their Sta. Rita Hills Chardonnay comes from a cool, windy pocket near the Pacific, so it keeps fresh acidity under its ripe fruit and gentle oak: California richness without heaviness.

domaine-durand.name: Domaine Durand
domaine-durand.line: A family estate in the Loire and Sancerre, run by brothers, making crisp everyday Sauvignon Blanc.
domaine-durand.tell: Domaine Durand is a family estate in the Loire. This Sauvignon Blanc is the region in a glass: crisp, citrusy and green-edged, unoaked and easy with salads, goat cheese and lighter fish.

minuty.name: Château Minuty
minuty.line: A Provence estate on the Saint-Tropez peninsula, known for pale, dry, Grenache-led rosé.
minuty.tell: Minuty is one of the best-known names in Provence rosé, from near Saint-Tropez. The Prestige is very pale, dry and delicate, with red berry and citrus, the classic poolside style that also flatters lighter Creole dishes.

domaine-de-durban.name: Domaine de Durban
domaine-de-durban.line: A hillside estate above Beaumes-de-Venise in the southern Rhône, famous for Muscat and also making Grenache-led reds.
domaine-de-durban.tell: Durban sits high above Beaumes-de-Venise, a village better known for sweet Muscat. Their red is Grenache-led: warm red fruit, a little spice and garrigue, and soft enough for a guest who wants something easy with meat.

moulin-d-issan.name: Moulin d'Issan
moulin-d-issan.line: A Bordeaux Supérieur from the family behind Château d'Issan in Margaux, made to drink young.
moulin-d-issan.tell: Moulin d'Issan comes from the people behind Château d'Issan in Margaux, made from vines outside the classed growth. It is a Cabernet-led claret with dark fruit and firm but friendly tannin, a true Bordeaux at a glass price.

damien-martin.name: Domaine Damien Martin
damien-martin.line: A family estate in Davayé in the Mâconnais, making straightforward Bourgogne for everyday drinking.
damien-martin.tell: Damien Martin is a family domaine in the south of Burgundy. This Bourgogne Pinot Noir is light and fruity, red cherry and strawberry with soft tannin, a gentle red for fish, chicken or a guest who wants red with a lighter dish.

inglenook.name: Inglenook
inglenook.line: A historic Rutherford estate restored by Francis Ford Coppola, whose flagship red is Rubicon.
inglenook.tell: Inglenook is one of Napa's historic estates in Rutherford, brought back together by Francis Ford Coppola. Rubicon is the flagship Cabernet blend, deep and structured; Blancaneaux is the estate's white blend, rounder and richer.

piper-heidsieck.name: Piper-Heidsieck
piper-heidsieck.line: A large Reims house with a fruity, Pinot Noir-led style; it makes Brennan's own Essential cuvée.
piper-heidsieck.tell: Piper-Heidsieck is a big Reims house with a generous, fruit-forward style led by Pinot Noir. Brennan's Essential is made for the house by Piper, an Extra Brut, so it is drier than most; the Sauvage rosé is fuller and fruitier.

rare-champagne.name: Rare Champagne
rare-champagne.line: Once Piper-Heidsieck's prestige cuvée, Rare is now its own label: vintage Champagne, rich and spicy, made only in chosen years.
rare-champagne.tell: Rare began as the prestige wine of Piper-Heidsieck and now stands on its own. It is made only in chosen vintages and aged long before release, so it tastes rich and layered, with toast, dried fruit and spice. A celebration bottle.

armand-de-brignac.name: Armand de Brignac
armand-de-brignac.line: The Champagne in the metallic gold "Ace of Spades" bottle, ripe and rich in style.
armand-de-brignac.tell: Armand de Brignac is the Ace of Spades, known on sight for its gold metallic bottle. The Gold Brut is ripe and full, with a creamy texture. Guests who ask for it usually want the bottle as much as the wine, so present it with ceremony.

ayala.name: Ayala
ayala.line: An Aÿ house owned by the Bollinger family since 2005, known for a pure, low-dosage, Chardonnay-driven style.
ayala.tell: Ayala is an old Aÿ house now in the Bollinger family. Its style is lean and pure, with little sugar added, so the wines taste crisp and precise. The Majeur rosé is dry and delicate, good with seafood.

billecart-salmon.name: Billecart-Salmon
billecart-salmon.line: A family-run house in Mareuil-sur-Aÿ, prized for finesse, freshness and one of Champagne's most admired rosés.
billecart-salmon.tell: Billecart-Salmon is still family run and loved for elegance: fine bubbles, fresh fruit and a clean finish. The rosé is the one guests know; Elisabeth Salmon is its prestige rosé, Nicolas François the prestige white, and Clos St Hilaire a rare single vineyard Pinot Noir.

bollinger.name: Bollinger
bollinger.line: A family house in Aÿ with a rich, Pinot Noir-led style shaped by barrel fermentation and long ageing.
bollinger.tell: Bollinger is Pinot Noir country Champagne: full, toasty and vinous, partly fermented in oak. Special Cuvée is the house blend, La Grande Année the vintage, R.D. a vintage aged long on its lees and disgorged late, and Vieilles Vignes Françaises a tiny, legendary Blanc de Noirs.

charles-heidsieck.name: Charles Heidsieck
charles-heidsieck.line: A Reims house famous for using a high share of old reserve wines, giving rich, toasty, creamy Champagne.
charles-heidsieck.tell: Charles Heidsieck ages its wines in old chalk cellars and blends in a lot of older reserve wine, so even the Brut Réserve tastes rich and toasty. Blanc des Millénaires is the long-aged prestige Blanc de Blancs; Champagne Charlie revives a historic name.

delamotte.name: Delamotte
delamotte.line: A small Le Mesnil-sur-Oger house, sister to Salon, devoted to Chardonnay from the Côte des Blancs.
delamotte.tell: Delamotte is Salon's sister house in Le Mesnil, heart of the Côte des Blancs. Its Blanc de Blancs is crisp, chalky and elegant, with lemon and brioche, a great step toward Salon's style at a gentler price.

deutz.name: Deutz
deutz.line: An Aÿ house, part of the Louis Roederer group, with a fine, elegant style.
deutz.tell: Deutz is an Aÿ house in the Roederer family of wines, known for finesse rather than power. The rosé is fresh and red-fruited, a lovely aperitif or partner for lighter seafood.

dom-perignon.name: Dom Pérignon
dom-perignon.line: Moët & Chandon's prestige vintage Champagne; the P2 release is held far longer on its lees.
dom-perignon.tell: Dom Pérignon is always a vintage and always a blend of Chardonnay and Pinot Noir. P2 is the same wine released at its second peak, after many more years on the lees, deeper and more toasty. The rosé is rarer still.

ruinart.name: Ruinart
ruinart.line: Founded in 1729 and often called the oldest established Champagne house, Ruinart is known for Chardonnay.
ruinart.tell: Ruinart dates to 1729 and leans on Chardonnay for a fresh, bright style. Dom Ruinart is the prestige vintage, a long-aged Blanc de Blancs, with a rosé version too. The house rosé is fruity and soft.

drappier.name: Drappier
drappier.line: A family house in the Aube, deep in Pinot Noir country, with a lightly dosed style and a love of large bottles.
drappier.tell: Drappier is a family house in the Côte des Bar in the south of Champagne, where Pinot Noir rules. The wines are fruit-driven and often low in added sugar; Brut Nature has none. Grande Sendrée is their prestige vintage.

duval-leroy.name: Duval-Leroy
duval-leroy.line: A family-owned house in Vertus at the south of the Côte des Blancs, with a Chardonnay-rich, elegant style.
duval-leroy.tell: Duval-Leroy is family owned, based in Vertus in the Côte des Blancs. Femme de Champagne is their prestige cuvée, long-aged and Chardonnay-led: creamy, refined and complex.

gosset.name: Gosset
gosset.line: An Aÿ house that traces its wine roots to 1584 and usually avoids malolactic fermentation, keeping wines taut and fresh.
gosset.tell: Gosset claims to be the oldest wine house in Champagne and makes wines with bright, firm acidity because it usually blocks the softening malolactic step. Grande Réserve is the house blend; Celebris is the prestige vintage. Ideal with rich food.

henriot.name: Henriot
henriot.line: A Reims family house with a Chardonnay-rich style, fine and lightly toasty.
henriot.tell: Henriot leans on Chardonnay for a fine, creamy, lightly toasty style. The Blanc de Blancs is crisp; the Millésime is the vintage; Cuvée des Enchanteleurs and Hemera are the long-aged prestige wines.

krug.name: Krug
krug.line: The Reims house that ferments in small oak casks and builds Grande Cuvée from many vintages, numbered by edition.
krug.tell: Krug is barrel-fermented and deeply complex, toasty, nutty and powerful. Grande Cuvée blends over a hundred wines from many years; the edition number tells you which. Clos du Mesnil and Clos d'Ambonnay are tiny walled vineyards, among Champagne's rarest bottles.

laurent-perrier.name: Laurent-Perrier
laurent-perrier.line: A Tours-sur-Marne house known for its rosé made by skin maceration and for Grand Siècle, a blend of three vintages.
laurent-perrier.tell: Laurent-Perrier is famous for its rosé, coloured by soaking Pinot Noir on its skins, and for Grand Siècle, which blends three great vintages; the Iteration number names the release. Harmony is a demi-sec, sweeter, for dessert.

louis-roederer.name: Louis Roederer
louis-roederer.line: A family-owned Reims house, maker of Cristal, with a precise, vinous style.
louis-roederer.tell: Roederer is family owned and farms most of its own vines. Cristal, first made for the Russian tsar, is the prestige wine: fine, chalky, long. Collection is the newer multi-vintage house blend, numbered by release.

moet-chandon.name: Moët & Chandon
moet-chandon.line: Champagne's largest house, in Épernay, with a bright, fruity style.
moet-chandon.tell: Moët is the largest Champagne house. Grand Vintage is its vintage wine, made only in chosen years, fuller and toastier than the Impérial. Nectar Impérial Rosé is sweeter, a demi-sec, for guests who like it softer or with dessert.

nicolas-feuillatte.name: Nicolas Feuillatte
nicolas-feuillatte.line: A large growers' cooperative brand in Chouilly, fresh and fruity, with Palmes d'Or as its prestige cuvée.
nicolas-feuillatte.tell: Nicolas Feuillatte brings together grapes from thousands of growers through a cooperative. The Réserve is fresh, fruity and approachable; Palmes d'Or is the prestige vintage in its studded bottle, and comes as a fuller rosé too.

perrier-jouet.name: Perrier-Jouët
perrier-jouet.line: An Épernay house with a floral, Chardonnay-led style; Belle Epoque wears the painted anemone bottle.
perrier-jouet.tell: Perrier-Jouët is all about elegance and flowers, built on Chardonnay. Belle Epoque, the vintage prestige wine in the anemone bottle, is the one guests recognise; it is delicate and creamy and photographs beautifully at the table.

philipponnat.name: Philipponnat
philipponnat.line: A Mareuil-sur-Aÿ house with a powerful, Pinot Noir-driven style, owner of the steep walled vineyard Clos des Goisses.
philipponnat.tell: Philipponnat makes structured, Pinot Noir-led Champagne. Clos des Goisses is its famous single walled vineyard on a very steep chalk slope by the Marne: rich, deep and long-lived. Royale Réserve is the house blend, full and food-friendly.

ployez-jacquemart.name: Ployez-Jacquemart
ployez-jacquemart.line: A small family house in Ludes on the Montagne de Reims, making long-aged, refined Champagne.
ployez-jacquemart.tell: Ployez-Jacquemart is a small family house on the Montagne de Reims. Liesse d'Harbonville is its prestige cuvée, aged long before release, so it shows toast, nuts and a fine, creamy mousse. A collector's bottle at less than the famous names.

pol-roger.name: Pol Roger
pol-roger.line: A family-owned Épernay house, elegant and fine, whose Sir Winston Churchill cuvée honours its most famous customer.
pol-roger.tell: Pol Roger is still family owned and known for fine, persistent bubbles. Churchill was a devoted customer, so the prestige cuvée bears his name: powerful, Pinot Noir-rich and long. The Brut and Blanc de Blancs are crisp and polished.

salon.name: Salon
salon.line: Single cru, single grape, single vintage: Salon is Chardonnay from Le Mesnil, made only in exceptional years.
salon.tell: Salon makes one wine: a Blanc de Blancs from Le Mesnil, only in the finest years and aged about a decade before release. It is intense, chalky and long, one of the rarest Champagnes. Delamotte is its sister house.

taittinger.name: Taittinger
taittinger.line: A Reims house with a Chardonnay-rich, light and elegant style; Comtes de Champagne is its Blanc de Blancs.
taittinger.tell: Taittinger favours Chardonnay, so its wines are light, fine and elegant. La Française is the house Brut; Comtes de Champagne, the prestige Blanc de Blancs, is creamy and refined; the Prestige rosé is fresh and fruity.

veuve-clicquot.name: Veuve Clicquot
veuve-clicquot.line: A Reims house led by Pinot Noir, named for the widow who ran it in the early 1800s; Yellow Label is its signature.
veuve-clicquot.tell: Veuve Clicquot is the orange label everyone knows, a Pinot Noir-led, round and fruity Brut. La Grande Dame, named for Madame Clicquot, is the prestige vintage, finer and longer; its rosé is a true celebration bottle.

charles-mignon.name: Charles Mignon
charles-mignon.line: A family house in Épernay making approachable, fruit-forward Champagne.
charles-mignon.tell: Charles Mignon is a family house in Épernay. Comte de Marne is its grand cru cuvée, rounder and fuller; the Premium Réserve rosé is soft and fruity. Good value against the big names.

lallier.name: Lallier
lallier.line: An Aÿ house making grand cru Champagne with Pinot Noir and Chardonnay at its heart.
lallier.tell: Lallier is based in Aÿ, a grand cru village for Pinot Noir. The wines are fresh and precise; Ouvrage is its top grand cru Extra Brut, dry and deep. Ask the sommelier what the date in brackets on the list means for this bottle.

aubry.name: Aubry
aubry.line: A family grower near Reims known for reviving Champagne's rare old grapes alongside the classic three.
aubry.tell: Aubry is a family estate just west of Reims, run by two brothers. They are known for growing Champagne's forgotten grapes such as Arbane and Petit Meslier alongside the classic ones, so their wines taste lively and a little different.

barnaut.name: Barnaut
barnaut.line: A grower in Bouzy, a grand cru village famed for Pinot Noir, making rich, red-fruited Champagne.
barnaut.tell: Barnaut farms in Bouzy, one of the great Pinot Noir villages. Their Blanc de Noirs, white wine from black grapes, is full and red-fruited, a Champagne with real body for richer dishes.

benoit-lahaye.name: Benoît Lahaye
benoit-lahaye.line: An organic grower in Bouzy making precise, low-dosage Champagne, much of it single-plot.
benoit-lahaye.tell: Benoît Lahaye farms organically in Bouzy and adds little or no sugar, so the wines are dry, vivid and true to place. Several bottles are single plots like Le Jardin de la Grosse Pierre. Ask the sommelier how Violaine is made.

chartogne-taillet.name: Chartogne-Taillet
chartogne-taillet.line: A grower in Merfy, northwest of Reims, known for single-parcel wines that show their soils.
chartogne-taillet.tell: Chartogne-Taillet is a family estate in Merfy, a quiet corner north of Reims. Alexandre Chartogne bottles single parcels such as Les Barres and Orizeaux separately, so each one shows its own soil. Sainte Anne is the fresh, approachable blend.

david-leclapart.name: David Leclapart
david-leclapart.line: A tiny biodynamic grower in Trépail making intense, mineral Blanc de Blancs.
david-leclapart.tell: David Leclapart farms biodynamically in Trépail, a Chardonnay outpost on the Montagne de Reims. His wines are low in dosage and very pure; L'Artiste and L'Apôtre are two of the cult names in grower Champagne, made in small amounts.

egly-ouriet.name: Egly-Ouriet
egly-ouriet.line: An Ambonnay grower making powerful, long-aged, Pinot Noir-rich Champagne, among the most sought after.
egly-ouriet.tell: Egly-Ouriet farms Ambonnay, a grand cru for Pinot Noir, and rests its wines a long time on their lees, so they taste deep and vinous. Les Crayères is an old-vine Blanc de Noirs and the Millésime is the vintage, a wine-lover's Champagne for rich dishes.

eric-rodez.name: Eric Rodez
eric-rodez.line: An Ambonnay grower working plot by plot, with some oak, for detailed grand cru Champagne.
eric-rodez.tell: Eric Rodez is a grower in Ambonnay who vinifies plot by plot and uses some oak. Empreinte Blanche is Chardonnay-led and fine; Les Genettes is a single site. Expect depth and detail rather than big-brand polish.

guy-mea.name: Guy Méa
guy-mea.line: A family estate in Louvois on the Montagne de Reims, blending Pinot Noir and Chardonnay from grand and premier cru villages.
guy-mea.tell: Guy Méa is a family estate in Louvois. L'Assemblage is a Pinot Noir-led blend with Chardonnay, low in dosage, with citrus, white flowers and a bready edge. A grower bottle at a fair price.

hure-freres.name: Huré Frères
hure-freres.line: A family grower in Ludes on the Montagne de Reims, run by siblings, with a fresh, precise style.
hure-freres.tell: Huré Frères is a family estate on the Montagne de Reims. 4 Éléments is a single-grape, single-site series; ask the sommelier which grape this bottle is. Low dosage, crisp and focused.

j-dumangin.name: J. Dumangin & Fils
j-dumangin.line: A family grower in Chigny-les-Roses making round, approachable Champagne at a fair price.
j-dumangin.tell: Dumangin is a family estate on the Montagne de Reims. The Brut is fruity, round and easy to love, a great grower Champagne for a guest who wants something beyond the big brands without paying a lot.

j-lassalle.name: J. Lassalle
j-lassalle.line: A family estate in Chigny-les-Roses, long run by the women of the family, with a fine, gentle style.
j-lassalle.tell: J. Lassalle is a small family house on the Montagne de Reims, known for finesse. The Special Club is their prestige bottle under the growers' club that sets a strict standard; the Blanc de Blancs is crisp and delicate.

lelarge-pugeot.name: Lelarge-Pugeot
lelarge-pugeot.line: An organic grower in Vrigny, west of Reims, known for wines that give Meunier a starring role.
lelarge-pugeot.tell: Lelarge-Pugeot farms organically in Vrigny. Les Meuniers de Clémence is a Blanc de Noirs from Meunier, the underrated grape of Champagne: fruity, open and generous, very good with food.

paul-bara.name: Paul Bara
paul-bara.line: A Bouzy grower devoted to rich, Pinot Noir-led grand cru Champagne.
paul-bara.tell: Paul Bara is a family estate in Bouzy, famous for Pinot Noir. The wines are full and red-fruited. The Special Club bottles, white and rosé, are their prestige wines, made under the growers' club rules.

francoise-bedel.name: Françoise Bedel
francoise-bedel.line: A biodynamic grower at the western end of the Marne valley, working mostly with Meunier.
francoise-bedel.tell: Françoise Bedel farms biodynamically in the far west of the Marne valley, where Meunier is king. The wines are generous, aromatic and long-aged before release. Originelle, Dis Vin Secret and Entre Ciel et Terre are three different blends.

caillez-lemaire.name: Caillez Lemaire
caillez-lemaire.line: A family grower in Damery in the Marne valley, with a low-dosage, Meunier-rich style.
caillez-lemaire.tell: Caillez Lemaire is a family estate in Damery. Pur is a Blanc de Noirs with no added sugar, crisp and fruity; Éclats is the blend, here in magnum, which suits a table of four or more.

famille-mousse.name: Famille Moussé
famille-mousse.line: A family grower in the Marne valley devoted to Meunier, making expressive Blanc de Noirs.
famille-mousse.tell: Moussé is a family estate in the Marne valley, champions of Meunier. Les Fortes Terres is a Blanc de Noirs: fruity, rounded and savoury. Good with fried seafood and richer starters.

gamet.name: Gamet
gamet.line: A family grower in the Marne valley; Rive Gauche is its left-bank blend, here in magnum.
gamet.tell: Gamet is a family estate in the Marne valley. Rive Gauche is a blend from the river's left bank, here in magnum. Ask the sommelier for the grape mix before you describe it in detail.

gaston-chiquet.name: Gaston Chiquet
gaston-chiquet.line: A Dizy family grower known for a rare Blanc de Blancs from Aÿ, a village planted mostly to Pinot Noir.
gaston-chiquet.tell: Gaston Chiquet is a family estate in Dizy. Their Blanc de Blancs d'Aÿ is unusual: Chardonnay from Aÿ, where Pinot Noir dominates, so it is fuller and rounder than a Côte des Blancs Chardonnay. Here in magnum.

goutorbe-bouillot.name: Goutorbe-Bouillot
goutorbe-bouillot.line: A family grower in Damery on the Marne making fruity, approachable blends.
goutorbe-bouillot.tell: Goutorbe-Bouillot is a family estate in Damery. Reflets de Rivière and Le Ru des Charmes are their blends, built on Pinot Noir and Meunier from the river valley: fruity, round and easy to enjoy.

henri-giraud.name: Henri Giraud
henri-giraud.line: An old Aÿ family house that ages its wines in oak from the nearby Argonne forest.
henri-giraud.tell: Henri Giraud is a family house in Aÿ that ferments and ages in casks made from Argonne oak, close to Champagne. The wines are rich, vinous and nutty; Argonne is the top cuvée and Fût de Chêne the oak-aged blend.

jm-seleque.name: JM Sélèque
jm-seleque.line: A young-generation grower in Pierry, near Épernay, making precise, single-parcel Champagne.
jm-seleque.tell: Jean-Marc Sélèque runs his family estate in Pierry and is one of the rising grower names. Solessence is the blend; the Soliste wines are single parcels and single grapes. Crisp, chalky and dry.

leclerc-briant.name: Leclerc Briant
leclerc-briant.line: An Épernay house that was an early convert to biodynamic farming, making pure, low-dosage wines.
leclerc-briant.tell: Leclerc Briant is an Épernay house known for organic and biodynamic farming. The wines are fresh and dry; Clos des Trois Clochers is a single walled vineyard with no added sugar; the Réserve, here in magnum, is the house blend.

marc-hebrart.name: Marc Hébrart
marc-hebrart.line: A family grower in Mareuil-sur-Aÿ; Rive Gauche Rive Droite blends grand cru vines from both banks of the Marne.
marc-hebrart.tell: Marc Hébrart is a much-admired grower in Mareuil-sur-Aÿ. Rive Gauche Rive Droite blends Pinot Noir and Chardonnay from both sides of the Marne: rich yet fresh, with real depth. Offered in bottle and magnum.

marie-noelle-ledru.name: Marie-Noëlle Ledru
marie-noelle-ledru.line: A small, much-loved grower in Ambonnay making intense, Pinot Noir-based grand cru Champagne.
marie-noelle-ledru.tell: Marie-Noëlle Ledru's wines come from Ambonnay in tiny amounts and are hard to find. Cuvée du Goulté is a Blanc de Noirs, rich and red-fruited. A collector's bottle; ask the sommelier about the vintage and its condition.

pierre-paillard.name: Pierre Paillard
pierre-paillard.line: A family estate in Bouzy making precise, low-dosage grand cru Champagne.
pierre-paillard.tell: Pierre Paillard is a family estate in Bouzy run by brothers. La Grande Récolte and Les Parcelles are dry, focused grand cru wines; Les Parcelles carries a number for its base year. Crisp and clean, very good with seafood.

rene-geoffroy.name: René Geoffroy
rene-geoffroy.region: Aÿ and Cumières, Vallée de la Marne
rene-geoffroy.line: A family grower rooted in Cumières, known for rich, vinous Champagne and a fine saignée rosé.
rene-geoffroy.tell: René Geoffroy is a family estate with deep roots in Cumières. Cuvée Expression is the round, fruity house blend, and the Rosé de Saignée is coloured on the skins: deep, fruity and great with food.

tribaut-schloesser.name: Tribaut-Schloesser
tribaut-schloesser.line: A family house in the Marne valley making approachable, fruit-forward Champagne.
tribaut-schloesser.tell: Tribaut-Schloesser is a family house in the Marne valley. Origine is a fruity, gentle blend, and here it comes as a half-bottle, the right size for one or two guests.

agrapart.name: Agrapart
agrapart.line: A celebrated Avize grower making mineral, low-dosage grand cru Blanc de Blancs.
agrapart.tell: Agrapart is one of the great grower names in Avize. The wines are pure Chardonnay, intense and chalky, often with little or no added sugar. A bottle for a guest who loves precise, serious Champagne.

brigitte-fallon.name: Brigitte Fallon (Michel Fallon)
brigitte-fallon.line: A tiny Avize label from Michel Fallon, who long worked at Jacques Selosse, making grand cru Blanc de Blancs.
brigitte-fallon.tell: Brigitte Fallon is a very small label made in Avize by Michel Fallon, whose experience comes from years in the Selosse cellar. It is a grand cru Blanc de Blancs, rich and precise. Production is tiny; the list spells it Bridgette.

dhondt-grellet.name: Dhondt-Grellet
dhondt-grellet.line: A young-generation grower in the Côte des Blancs making precise, single-site Chardonnay Champagne.
dhondt-grellet.tell: Dhondt-Grellet is a family estate in the Côte des Blancs, now run by Adrien Dhondt. Les Nogers and Les Terres Fines are single sites; Le Bateau and Dans un Premier Temps are the blends. Dry, chalky, lively.

diebolt-vallois.name: Diebolt-Vallois
diebolt-vallois.line: A family grower in Cramant making fine, creamy Blanc de Blancs.
diebolt-vallois.tell: Diebolt-Vallois is a family estate in Cramant, a grand cru for Chardonnay. The Blanc de Blancs is fine, floral and creamy; here in magnum for a larger table.

doyard.name: Doyard
doyard.line: A family grower in Vertus making traditional, oak-touched Chardonnay Champagne.
doyard.tell: Doyard is a family estate in Vertus. Vendémiaire is a premier cru Blanc de Blancs, partly oak-aged, with a rich, nutty side to its crisp fruit.

gonet-medeville.name: Gonet-Médeville
gonet-medeville.line: A family grower whose family also owns property in Sauternes, making textured, food-friendly Champagne.
gonet-medeville.tell: Gonet-Médeville joins a Champagne family and a Bordeaux one. Champ d'Alouette is a single site Extra Brut, dry, deep and vinous, made for the table rather than the toast.

jacques-selosse.name: Jacques Selosse
jacques-selosse.line: Anselme Selosse's Avize estate, the most influential grower in modern Champagne, making rich, oxidative, barrel-aged wines.
jacques-selosse.tell: Selosse changed grower Champagne: barrel-fermented, bold, nutty and savoury, almost like great white Burgundy with bubbles. Substance is built from a perpetual reserve and Initial is the entry Blanc de Blancs; the date the list prints in brackets is the disgorgement.

guillaume-selosse.name: Guillaume Selosse
guillaume-selosse.line: Anselme Selosse's son, who makes small lots under his own name.
guillaume-selosse.tell: Guillaume Selosse is Anselme's son and makes his own wines in tiny amounts. Largillier is a rosé, and the date in brackets on the list is its disgorgement, so this is a rare find for a guest who already knows the Selosse name.

jl-vergnon.name: JL Vergnon
jl-vergnon.line: A Le Mesnil grower making razor-sharp, low-dosage grand cru Blanc de Blancs.
jl-vergnon.tell: JL Vergnon makes Chardonnay from Le Mesnil, some of the most chalky ground in Champagne. Les Hautes Mottes is a Brut Nature, no sugar added, so it is bone-dry and electric. Lovely with oysters.

larmandier-bernier.name: Larmandier-Bernier
larmandier-bernier.line: A biodynamic family estate in Vertus making pure, low-dosage Chardonnay Champagne.
larmandier-bernier.tell: Larmandier-Bernier is a leading biodynamic grower in Vertus. Longitude is a crisp, chalky Blanc de Blancs; Terre de Vertus is a single-village Brut Nature, bone-dry and intense. Superb with shellfish.

legras-haas.name: Legras & Haas
legras-haas.line: A family estate in Chouilly making fresh grand cru Chardonnay Champagne and rosé.
legras-haas.tell: Legras & Haas is a family house in Chouilly, a grand cru for Chardonnay. The Blanc de Blancs is fresh and fine; the Millésime is its vintage; Intuition and the Rosé add red fruit.

philippe-gonet.name: Philippe Gonet
philippe-gonet.line: A family house in Le Mesnil with Chardonnay at its core, from fresh blends to grand cru vintage.
philippe-gonet.tell: Philippe Gonet is a family house in Le Mesnil. TER is a Blanc de Blancs, the Réserve a blend and the Millésime a grand cru vintage Blanc de Blancs. Crisp, chalky and good value for its villages.

pierre-cellier.name: Pierre Cellier
pierre-cellier.line: A label from the Gonet family of Le Mesnil, first made for a Paris restaurant friend in the 1970s.
pierre-cellier.tell: Pierre Cellier comes from the Gonet family in Le Mesnil. Cuvée Prestige is a Pinot Noir-led blend with Chardonnay from Le Mesnil: round, toasty and fruity, a crowd-pleaser.

pierre-peters.name: Pierre Péters
pierre-peters.line: A leading Le Mesnil grower whose Blanc de Blancs draws on a long-kept perpetual reserve.
pierre-peters.tell: Pierre Péters is one of the benchmark growers of Le Mesnil. Cuvée de Réserve blends young wine with a perpetual reserve, giving depth to its chalky freshness. Les Montjolys and Réserve Oubliée are the top bottles.

roland-champion.name: Roland Champion
roland-champion.line: A family grower in Chouilly making grand cru Blanc de Blancs.
roland-champion.tell: Roland Champion is a family estate in Chouilly. Grand Éclat is a grand cru Blanc de Blancs, here in a six-litre Methuselah, a bottle for a big celebration that needs planning with the sommelier.

stephane-coquillette.name: Stéphane Coquillette
stephane-coquillette.line: A small family grower in the Côte des Blancs area making approachable Champagne and rosé.
stephane-coquillette.tell: Stéphane Coquillette is a small grower. The Brut is fresh and fruity; Marie Aimer is a rosé. Ask the sommelier about the grapes before going into detail.

varnier-fanniere.name: Varnier-Fannière
varnier-fanniere.line: A small grower in Avize making fine grand cru Chardonnay Champagne.
varnier-fanniere.tell: Varnier-Fannière is a small family estate in Avize, a grand cru village for Chardonnay. Their Brut is crisp, fine and chalky, a true grower wine at a fair price.

veuve-fourny.name: Veuve Fourny & Fils
veuve-fourny.line: A family house in Vertus run by two brothers, making crisp, low-dosage premier cru Chardonnay.
veuve-fourny.tell: Veuve Fourny is a family house in Vertus. The wines are dry and chalky; Monts de Vertus is a single site; the half-bottles suit one or two guests; Vinothèque MV2000 is a perpetual-reserve blend in magnum.

waris-larmandier.name: Waris-Larmandier
waris-larmandier.line: A family grower in the Côte des Blancs making precise, low-dosage grand cru Champagne.
waris-larmandier.tell: Waris-Larmandier is a small family estate in the Côte des Blancs. Les Bauves is a single site, Brut Nature, bone-dry and chalky; L'Instant de Passions is a rosé. Ask the sommelier which grand cru village it comes from.

brocard-pierre.name: Pierre Brocard
brocard-pierre.line: A grower in the Côte des Bar, the Pinot Noir country in the south of Champagne.
brocard-pierre.tell: Pierre Brocard farms in the Aube. Saignée de la Côte is a rosé made by bleeding juice off Pinot Noir skins, so it is deep in colour and full of red fruit, a rosé Champagne with body for food.

clandestin.name: Clandestin
clandestin.line: A small house in the Aube founded by Burgundian Benoît Doussot, working with organic growers and adding no dosage.
clandestin.tell: Clandestin is Benoît Doussot's project in the Côte des Bar. He buys from about a dozen organic growers, ferments in barrel and adds no sugar. Les Semblables and Les Grandes Lignes are single-grape wines; dry, vinous, food-friendly.

jean-laurent.name: Jean Laurent
jean-laurent.line: A family grower in the Aube making Pinot Noir and Chardonnay Champagne, including rosé.
jean-laurent.tell: Jean Laurent is a family estate in the Côte des Bar. The rosé is fruity and full; the Blanc de Blancs, here in magnum, is fresher. Good value next to the big houses.

argyle.name: Argyle
argyle.line: A Dundee Hills winery built around traditional method sparkling wine, one of Oregon's pioneers in the style.
argyle.tell: Argyle makes sparkling wine the Champagne way in Oregon. The Brut is crisp and appley; Extended Tirage spends longer on its lees, toastier; Julia Lee's Block is a single vineyard Blanc de Blancs. An American bubble with real finesse.

jansz.name: Jansz
jansz.line: A Tasmanian sparkling specialist using cool-climate fruit for traditional method wine.
jansz.tell: Jansz is a Tasmanian sparkling house. The island's cool climate keeps acidity bright, so the Premier Cuvée is fresh and creamy, made the Champagne way at a friendly price.

brundlmayer.name: Bründlmayer
brundlmayer.line: A leading Kamptal estate in Langenlois, famous for Riesling from the Heiligenstein and Grüner Veltliner, plus fine sparkling wine.
brundlmayer.tell: Bründlmayer is one of Austria's great names. The Heiligenstein Rieslings are taut and mineral, the Grüner Veltliners peppery and fresh. Their sparkling wine is made the Champagne way and is among the best outside Champagne.

schloss-gobelsburg.name: Schloss Gobelsburg
schloss-gobelsburg.line: A historic Kamptal estate with monastic roots, known for Riesling, Grüner Veltliner and the old-style Tradition wines.
schloss-gobelsburg.tell: Schloss Gobelsburg is a historic estate in the Kamptal. The Heiligenstein Riesling is mineral and fine; Tradition is a Grüner-based wine made in an old-fashioned way, aged long in big casks. Their Brut is crisp and elegant.

ridgeview.name: Ridgeview
ridgeview.line: A family winery in Sussex making English sparkling wine from the Champagne grapes.
ridgeview.tell: Ridgeview is a Sussex family estate, part of England's sparkling success. Bloomsbury is Chardonnay-led and fresh, Cavendish Pinot-led and rounder, Fitzrovia a rosé. A fun surprise for a guest who has never tried English bubbles.

luis-pato.name: Luis Pato
luis-pato.line: A Bairrada estate known for single vineyard wines and sparkling wine from local grapes.
luis-pato.tell: Luis Pato is a leading name in Bairrada. Vinha Formal and Vinha Pan are named for single vineyards and both come in magnum. Ask the sommelier about the grapes and style of each before you describe them.

domaine-du-pelican.name: Domaine du Pélican
domaine-du-pelican.line: The Jura estate of Marquis d'Angerville of Volnay, making Chardonnay, Savagnin, Vin Jaune and sparkling wine.
domaine-du-pelican.tell: Domaine du Pélican is the Jura home of the d'Angerville family from Volnay. Grand Curoulet is a precise Chardonnay; the Savagnin Ouillé is topped up and fresh; the Vin Jaune is aged under a veil of yeast, nutty and intense.

ca-del-bosco.name: Ca' del Bosco
ca-del-bosco.line: A leading Franciacorta house making traditional method sparkling wine in Lombardy.
ca-del-bosco.tell: Ca' del Bosco is one of the great names of Franciacorta, Italy's answer to Champagne. Annamaria Clementi is the top wine, a Riserva aged long on its lees; this one has no added sugar.

caneva-da-nani.name: Caneva da Nani
caneva-da-nani.line: A small Veneto grower making col fondo, a lightly sparkling wine finished in the bottle with its lees left in.
caneva-da-nani.tell: Caneva da Nani makes col fondo in the Veneto: the Prosecco grape refermented in the bottle and left with its lees, so it can be cloudy, dry and lightly fizzy. A rustic, food-friendly sparkler.

ferrari.name: Ferrari
ferrari.line: A family-owned house in Trento making traditional method sparkling wine from mountain vineyards.
ferrari.tell: Ferrari, no relation to the cars, is Trento's great sparkling house. The Brut is crisp and appley; Perlé is a vintage Blanc de Blancs; the Rosé is fruity and dry. The half-bottle suits one or two.

domaine-carneros.name: Domaine Carneros
domaine-carneros.line: Taittinger's California estate in Carneros, making elegant traditional method sparkling wine.
domaine-carneros.tell: Domaine Carneros was founded by the Taittinger family in Carneros. Le Rêve is its prestige Blanc de Blancs, creamy, fine and long. A good bridge for a guest who loves Taittinger.

racines.name: Racines
racines.line: A Sta. Rita Hills project making cool-climate Chardonnay, Pinot Noir and sparkling wine.
racines.tell: Racines makes taut, cool-climate wines in Sta. Rita Hills, where Pacific wind keeps the grapes fresh. The Chardonnay is lean and mineral rather than buttery, and the Brut is crisp; ask the sommelier about the team behind it before telling the story.

roederer-estate.name: Roederer Estate
roederer-estate.line: Louis Roederer's California estate in the cool Anderson Valley, making refined sparkling wine.
roederer-estate.tell: Roederer Estate is the California home of the Champagne house Louis Roederer, in the cool Anderson Valley. L'Ermitage is its prestige wine; the rosé is fine and red-fruited.

schramsberg.name: Schramsberg
schramsberg.line: A historic Calistoga estate devoted to traditional method sparkling wine.
schramsberg.tell: Schramsberg is a Napa sparkling estate with historic caves. The Blanc de Blancs is crisp and lively, here in half-bottle; J. Schram is the prestige wine, richer and longer.

under-the-wire.name: Under the Wire
under-the-wire.line: A small California project bottling single vineyard sparkling wines, from the team at Bedrock Wine Co.
under-the-wire.tell: Under the Wire makes single vineyard sparkling wine in tiny lots. Alder Springs is a cool, high Mendocino site; the wine is an Extra Brut, dry and focused.

michel-bregeon.name: Michel Brégeon
michel-bregeon.line: A Muscadet estate known for long lees ageing, especially from the Gorges cru.
michel-bregeon.tell: Brégeon is a Muscadet estate that ages its wines a long time on their lees. Gorges is one of the new Muscadet crus, and long ageing gives it depth and a savoury, saline edge. Muscadet with oysters is a classic.

domaine-de-la-pepiere.name: Domaine de la Pépière
domaine-de-la-pepiere.line: A benchmark Muscadet estate making crisp, mineral, long-lived wines from old vines and named crus.
domaine-de-la-pepiere.tell: Pépière is one of the estates that made people take Muscadet seriously. Château-Thébaud and Monnières-Saint-Fiacre are crus, aged longer on their lees: crisp, saline and deep. Perfect with raw oysters; magnums suit a table.

jean-baptiste-hardy.name: Jean-Baptiste Hardy
jean-baptiste-hardy.region: Mouzillon, Muscadet Sèvre et Maine, Loire
jean-baptiste-hardy.line: A young vigneron who took over his family vines in Mouzillon in 2018, after training in Burgundy.
jean-baptiste-hardy.tell: Jean-Baptiste Hardy came home to his family's Muscadet vines after working in Burgundy. Fief de Chaintre is his top wine from an old plot, aged on its lees: textured, saline and serious Muscadet.

domaine-de-l-ecu.name: Domaine de l'Ecu
domaine-de-l-ecu.line: A biodynamic Muscadet estate that bottles by soil type; Orthogneiss is named for its rock.
domaine-de-l-ecu.tell: Domaine de l'Ecu farms biodynamically and bottles its Muscadets by soil. Orthogneiss is named for the rock under the vines and is deep, mineral and long. A Muscadet to convert a guest.

chateau-du-breuil.name: Châteaux du Breuil et de la Roche
chateau-du-breuil.line: An organic Anjou estate with a Savennières plot, focused on dry Chenin Blanc.
chateau-du-breuil.tell: This organic estate in Anjou has a parcel in Savennières and is serious about dry Chenin Blanc. Clos du Breuil is dry, textured and mineral. The list prints Château de La Roche; ask the sommelier if a guest asks about the name.

clau-de-nell.name: Clau de Nell
clau-de-nell.line: A small biodynamic estate in Anjou, owned by the Leflaive family of Burgundy.
clau-de-nell.tell: Clau de Nell is a small biodynamic estate in Anjou owned by the Leflaive family of Burgundy. Fontene is Chenin Blanc: dry, textured and precise, lovely with rich fish.

clos-rougeard.name: Clos Rougeard
clos-rougeard.line: The legendary Saumur estate of the Foucault brothers; Brézé is its rare, long-lived Chenin Blanc.
clos-rougeard.tell: Clos Rougeard is a cult name in the Loire. Brézé is its white, Chenin Blanc from a famous Saumur hillside: dry, powerful and built to age. A rare bottle for a collector.

domaine-des-baumard.name: Domaine des Baumard
domaine-des-baumard.line: An Anjou family estate known for Savennières and sweet Quarts de Chaume.
domaine-des-baumard.tell: Baumard is a family estate in Anjou. Their Savennières is dry Chenin Blanc, firm, honeyed and mineral, best with rich fish, crab or chicken.

damien-laureau.name: Damien Laureau
damien-laureau.line: A small Savennières grower making precise, dry Chenin Blanc.
damien-laureau.tell: Damien Laureau is a small grower in Savennières. L'Alliance is dry Chenin Blanc, taut and mineral, with apple and honey and a long finish. Good with rich fish.

nicolas-joly.name: Nicolas Joly
nicolas-joly.line: The biodynamic pioneer of Savennières, owner of the monopole Coulée de Serrant.
nicolas-joly.tell: Nicolas Joly is the great champion of biodynamics, and Coulée de Serrant is a vineyard he owns outright. The wines are powerful, dry Chenin Blanc, golden and honeyed, and they often benefit from air: ask the sommelier about decanting.

domaine-du-petit-metris.name: Domaine du Petit Métris
domaine-du-petit-metris.line: A family estate in Anjou making Savennières and sweet Chenin Blanc.
domaine-du-petit-metris.tell: Petit Métris is a family estate in Anjou. Les Fougeraies is a dry Savennières: Chenin Blanc with apple, honey and a stony finish, a serious white for rich fish.

champalou.name: Champalou
champalou.line: A family estate in Vouvray making pure Chenin Blanc in dry and off-dry styles.
champalou.tell: Champalou is a family estate in Vouvray. Their wine is Chenin Blanc, fresh, floral and gently fruity. Ask the sommelier whether this bottle is dry or off-dry before promising a guest either.

clos-thierriere.name: Clos Thierrière
clos-thierriere.line: A small Vouvray name making Chenin Blanc.
clos-thierriere.tell: This is Vouvray, Chenin Blanc from the middle Loire, where wines run from dry to sweet. Les Pleurs is a single cuvée; ask the sommelier how dry it is before you describe it to a guest.

domaine-huet.name: Domaine Huet
domaine-huet.line: Vouvray's reference estate, biodynamic, bottling three great vineyards from dry to sweet.
domaine-huet.tell: Huet is the name in Vouvray. It bottles three vineyards, Le Haut-Lieu, Le Mont and Clos du Bourg, and each comes Sec (dry), Demi-Sec (gently sweet) or Moelleux (sweet). Always say which style before pouring; the sweeter ones love spice.

pascal-janvier.name: Pascal Janvier
pascal-janvier.line: A small grower in Jasnières, a little-known Loire corner for crisp, dry Chenin Blanc.
pascal-janvier.tell: Pascal Janvier makes Chenin Blanc in Jasnières, a tiny, cool appellation north of Tours. The wines are dry, sharp and mineral. A great discovery for a guest who likes crisp whites.

henri-bourgeois.name: Henri Bourgeois
henri-bourgeois.line: A large family house in Chavignol making Sauvignon Blanc across Sancerre and nearby appellations.
henri-bourgeois.tell: Henri Bourgeois is a family house in Sancerre country. This bottle sits under Menetou-Salon on the list, a neighbour of Sancerre: crisp, citrusy Sauvignon Blanc at a gentler price.

francois-chidaine.name: François Chidaine
francois-chidaine.line: A biodynamic grower and the leading name in Montlouis, making dry and sweet Chenin Blanc.
francois-chidaine.tell: Chidaine is the star of Montlouis, across the river from Vouvray. Les Tuffeaux is Chenin Blanc, often with a touch of sweetness; ask the sommelier how dry this vintage is. Lovely with spiced dishes.

didier-dagueneau.name: Didier Dagueneau
didier-dagueneau.line: The most celebrated name in Pouilly-Fumé, making intense, barrel-fermented Sauvignon Blanc.
didier-dagueneau.tell: Dagueneau made Pouilly-Fumé famous among collectors; his son Louis-Benjamin now runs it. Pur Sang is Sauvignon Blanc of real intensity, smoky and long. Far beyond everyday Sauvignon.

domaine-vacheron.name: Domaine Vacheron
domaine-vacheron.line: A biodynamic family estate in Sancerre making precise, single-site Sauvignon Blanc and Pinot Noir.
domaine-vacheron.tell: Vacheron is a biodynamic family estate in Sancerre. Le Paradis is a single site Sauvignon Blanc with more depth and minerals than most Sancerre, lovely with goat cheese and fish.

vatan.name: Edmond et Anne Vatan
vatan.line: A tiny, revered Chavignol estate whose Clos la Néore is one of Sancerre's most sought-after wines.
vatan.tell: Vatan is tiny and revered. Clos la Néore is Sancerre of great depth, made traditionally, with more texture and age-worthiness than most. Here in magnum, a rare find.

pascal-cotat.name: Pascal Cotat
pascal-cotat.line: A traditional Chavignol grower bottling Sancerre from the steep Monts Damnés and Grande Côte hillsides.
pascal-cotat.tell: Pascal Cotat makes old-school Sancerre from Chavignol's steepest slopes. Monts Damnés and La Grande Côte are rich and ripe, sometimes with a hint of sweetness. His rosé, labelled by lot, is a rare treat.

roc-de-l-abbaye.name: Roc de l'Abbaye
roc-de-l-abbaye.line: A Pouilly-Fumé, Sauvignon Blanc from the right bank of the upper Loire.
roc-de-l-abbaye.tell: Pouilly-Fumé faces Sancerre across the Loire. This is crisp Sauvignon Blanc with citrus and a smoky, flinty edge, a good value step up from house white.

lucien-crochet.name: Lucien Crochet
lucien-crochet.line: A family estate in Bué, in the heart of Sancerre, making crisp whites and fine Pinot Noir rosé.
lucien-crochet.tell: Lucien Crochet is a family estate in Sancerre. Their rosé is Pinot Noir: pale, dry and delicate, with red berries and citrus, offered in bottle and magnum, and very friendly with food.

raveneau.name: Domaine François Raveneau
raveneau.line: The most revered estate in Chablis, making long-lived grand and premier cru wines in tiny amounts.
raveneau.tell: Raveneau is Chablis's most sought-after name. The wines are intense, mineral and built to age, from crus like Montée de Tonnerre, Butteaux and Blanchot. Rare and allocated: treat each bottle as a collector's.

dauvissat.name: Domaine René et Vincent Dauvissat
dauvissat.line: A great traditional Chablis estate, with Raveneau the reference for the region.
dauvissat.tell: Dauvissat stands beside Raveneau at the top of Chablis. The wines are aged partly in old barrels and taste pure, deep and stony. Les Clos and Les Preuses are grand crus; Vaillons a premier cru; Petit Chablis the entry.

william-fevre.name: Domaine William Fèvre
william-fevre.line: A major Chablis estate with a large holding of grand crus, making precise, mineral wines.
william-fevre.tell: William Fèvre owns a big share of Chablis's grand crus. The wines are crisp and stony with gentle oak. Bougros Côte Bouguerots is a steep part of Bougros; Preuses and Valmur are grand crus too.

droin.name: Jean-Paul et Benoît Droin
droin.line: A long-established family estate in Chablis making grand and premier cru wines with some oak.
droin.tell: Droin is an old family estate in Chablis. Valmur and Vaudésir are grand crus, richer and deeper; Montée de Tonnerre, Montmains and Vaillons are premier crus. Hommage à Louis honours a family elder.

domaine-gautheron.name: Domaine Alain Gautheron
domaine-gautheron.line: A family estate in Chablis making crisp, mineral wines up to grand cru.
domaine-gautheron.tell: Gautheron is a family estate in Chablis. Bougros and Preuses are grand crus, richer and longer than village Chablis but still crisp and stony; the Bourgogne is the easy entry.

jean-collet.name: Domaine Jean Collet et Fils
jean-collet.line: A family estate in Chablis with grand and premier cru holdings.
jean-collet.tell: Collet is a family estate in Chablis. Valmur is a grand cru, Vaillons a premier cru, here in magnum; the village Chablis is crisp and fresh.

louis-michel.name: Domaine Louis Michel
louis-michel.line: A Chablis estate that ages in steel rather than oak, giving pure, crisp, mineral wines.
louis-michel.tell: Louis Michel uses no oak, so the wines are pure Chablis: crisp, lemony and stony. Grenouilles is a grand cru; Montmains a premier cru in half-bottle. Ideal with oysters and shellfish.

domaine-vocoret.name: Domaine Vocoret et Fils
domaine-vocoret.line: A long-established family estate in Chablis.
domaine-vocoret.tell: Vocoret is a family estate in Chablis. Les Clos is the great grand cru, rich and powerful for Chablis; the village wine is crisp and fresh.

eleni-edouard-vocoret.name: Domaine Eleni et Edouard Vocoret
eleni-edouard-vocoret.line: A young couple's estate in Chablis making precise, organic-leaning premier crus.
eleni-edouard-vocoret.tell: Eleni and Edouard Vocoret started their own estate in Chablis. Butteaux and Forêts are premier crus, Bas de Chapelot a village site. Pure, crisp and stony.

gerard-duplessis.name: Gérard Duplessis
gerard-duplessis.line: A small, traditional Chablis estate making long-lived wines.
gerard-duplessis.tell: Duplessis is a small, traditional estate. Les Clos is a grand cru; Mont de Milieu and Montmains premier crus. The wines are firm and slow to open.

la-chablisienne.name: La Chablisienne
la-chablisienne.line: The Chablis cooperative, a large and reliable producer from village to grand cru.
la-chablisienne.tell: La Chablisienne is the cooperative of Chablis, a large and reliable producer. Grenouilles is a grand cru and Vaillons a premier cru: classic, crisp Chablis at a fair price.

louis-jadot.name: Louis Jadot
louis-jadot.line: A major Beaune négociant and grower whose range runs from Chablis to the grand crus of the Côte de Beaune.
louis-jadot.tell: Jadot is one of Burgundy's great houses. Its whites run from Chablis through Meursault and Puligny to Chevalier-Montrachet Les Demoiselles. Reliable and classic: a safe name for a guest who wants great white Burgundy.

albert-bichot.name: Albert Bichot
albert-bichot.line: A large Beaune house with estates across Burgundy, including Domaine Long-Depaquit in Chablis.
albert-bichot.tell: Albert Bichot is a big Beaune house with several estates. La Moutonne is a Chablis grand cru vineyard of Long-Depaquit, its Chablis estate. Ask the sommelier about each Bichot bottle's estate.

patrick-piuze.name: Patrick Piuze
patrick-piuze.line: A Québec-born winemaker making precise, site-driven Chablis from bought-in grapes.
patrick-piuze.tell: Patrick Piuze buys grapes from chosen plots across Chablis and bottles them site by site. Bougros is a grand cru; the Côtes d'Auxerre and Tonnerre wines come from just outside Chablis. Pure and mineral.

roland-lavantureux.name: Roland Lavantureux
roland-lavantureux.line: A family estate in Chablis making crisp, pure wines, including grand crus.
roland-lavantureux.tell: Lavantureux is a family estate in Chablis. Bougros, Preuses and Vaudésir are grand crus and Vau de Vey is a premier cru: clean, stony and precise.

billaud-simon.name: Billaud-Simon
billaud-simon.line: A historic Chablis estate known for pure, crisp wines, now owned by Faiveley.
billaud-simon.tell: Billaud-Simon is a historic Chablis estate, now owned by Faiveley. Vaillons is a premier cru, and the village Chablis, also in magnum, is crisp, fresh and lemony.

domaine-de-la-mandeliere.name: Domaine de la Mandelière
domaine-de-la-mandeliere.line: A Chablis estate; Les Fourneaux is a premier cru, here in magnum.
domaine-de-la-mandeliere.tell: This is a Chablis premier cru, Les Fourneaux, in magnum. Expect crisp, stony Chardonnay without heavy oak, a good bottle to share around a table of oysters.

guy-robin.name: Domaine Guy Robin
guy-robin.line: A traditional Chablis estate known for old vines.
guy-robin.tell: Guy Robin is a traditional estate. Valmur is a grand cru; the Vieilles Vignes Chablis comes from old vines, with more depth than most village wine.

laroche.name: Domaine Laroche
laroche.line: A large, well-known Chablis estate making wines from village to grand cru.
laroche.tell: Laroche is a major Chablis name. L'Homme Mort is a part of the Fourchaume premier cru, and the wine is crisp, citrusy and mineral, a classic with shellfish.

laurent-tribut.name: Laurent Tribut
laurent-tribut.line: A tiny, traditional Chablis estate making pure, quiet wines.
laurent-tribut.tell: Laurent Tribut is a small, traditional Chablis grower. Beauroy is a premier cru and the village Chablis is crisp and mineral, quiet wines that reward attention.

les-hauts-de-milly.name: Les Hauts de Milly
les-hauts-de-milly.line: A Chablis estate based in Milly; Côte de Léchet is a premier cru on the slopes above the village.
les-hauts-de-milly.tell: This is Chablis premier cru from Côte de Léchet, on the slopes above the village of Milly. Crisp, lemony and stony, it suits oysters and lighter fish.

moreau-naudet.name: Moreau-Naudet
moreau-naudet.line: A family estate in Chablis making ripe yet mineral wines.
moreau-naudet.tell: Moreau-Naudet is a family estate in Chablis. Forêts, Montmains and Vaillons are premier crus, and the village Chablis and Petit Chablis are fresh, crisp entries.

alice-olivier-de-moor.name: Alice et Olivier De Moor
alice-olivier-de-moor.line: A small organic estate in Courgis making natural-leaning Chablis and Aligoté.
alice-olivier-de-moor.tell: The De Moors farm organically and make wines with little intervention. Mont de Milieu is a premier cru; Bel Air et Clardy and L'Humeur du Temps are Chablis; Plantation 1902 is an old-vine Aligoté.

chateau-de-beru.name: Château de Béru
chateau-de-beru.line: A biodynamic family estate in Béru, at the edge of Chablis.
chateau-de-beru.tell: Château de Béru farms biodynamically at the edge of Chablis. Clos de Béru is a walled vineyard the estate owns alone, Montserre another site and Athénaïs a Bourgogne: precise and stony.

domaine-de-l-enclos.name: Domaine de l'Enclos
domaine-de-l-enclos.tell: This is village Chablis from a family estate. It is crisp, lemony and stony Chardonnay, an easy partner for oysters and lighter seafood.

gilbert-picq.name: Gilbert Picq et ses Fils
gilbert-picq.line: A family estate in Chichée making crisp Chablis.
gilbert-picq.tell: Picq is a family estate in Chichée, near Chablis. Their village Chablis is crisp, fresh and mineral, a classic with raw oysters.

de-villaine.name: A. et P. de Villaine
de-villaine.line: Aubert de Villaine's own estate in Bouzeron, known for Aligoté and Rully.
de-villaine.tell: This is the estate of Aubert de Villaine, long co-director of Domaine de la Romanée-Conti. The Bouzeron is Aligoté, crisp and fresh; the Rully wines are Chardonnay. Great value from a great name.

bernard-bonin.name: Bernard Bonin
bernard-bonin.line: A small Meursault estate making textured, precise wines.
bernard-bonin.tell: Bernard Bonin is a small Meursault estate. Genevrières and Charmes are premier crus; Clos du Cromin, La Rencontre and Les Tillets village sites; Initiales is Bourgogne.

bouard-bonnefoy.name: Bouard-Bonnefoy
bouard-bonnefoy.line: A family estate in Chassagne-Montrachet making precise whites.
bouard-bonnefoy.tell: Bouard-Bonnefoy is a family estate in Chassagne-Montrachet. Les Macherelles and Les Petits Clos Morgeot are premier crus, Le Charmois a Saint-Aubin premier cru, and the Aligoté and Bourgogne are value bottles.

bruno-colin.name: Bruno Colin
bruno-colin.line: A Chassagne estate, part of the Colin family.
bruno-colin.tell: Bruno Colin is part of the Colin family of Chassagne-Montrachet. His Chassagne is rich and nutty Chardonnay, and the Bourgogne is a simpler, fresher entry.

coche-dury.name: Domaine Coche-Dury
coche-dury.line: A legendary Meursault estate whose whites are among the rarest and most sought-after in the world.
coche-dury.tell: Coche-Dury is a cult name in Meursault: tiny volumes, huge demand, and a smoky, flinty edge over deep fruit. Even the Bourgogne is a collector's bottle, and the Corton-Charlemagne is the summit, so involve the sommelier on any of them.

alex-moreau.name: Domaine Alex Moreau
alex-moreau.line: Alex Moreau's own label, alongside his family's Domaine Bernard Moreau in Chassagne.
alex-moreau.tell: Alex Moreau is one of the brothers behind Bernard Moreau. His wines are precise and fresh. Les Champs Gain, La Maltroie and Morgeot are premier crus.

bernard-moreau.name: Domaine Bernard Moreau et Fils
bernard-moreau.line: A leading Chassagne estate making taut, precise whites.
bernard-moreau.tell: Bernard Moreau is a top Chassagne estate run by brothers, with taut, precise whites. La Maltroie, Les Chenevottes and Morgeot are premier crus, and Bâtard-Montrachet is the grand cru.

anne-gros.name: Domaine Anne Gros
anne-gros.line: A Vosne-Romanée estate best known for red, also making a fine Bourgogne Blanc.
anne-gros.tell: Anne Gros is a Vosne-Romanée estate famous for silky reds. Her white Bourgogne is fresh and elegant, a gentle way into a great name.

faiveley.name: Domaine Faiveley
faiveley.line: A large family estate in Nuits-Saint-Georges with vineyards from the Côte de Nuits to the Côte Chalonnaise.
faiveley.tell: Faiveley is a big family domaine based in Nuits-Saint-Georges. Clos Rochette Mercurey and Les Marnes Blanches Ladoix are value whites, while its Puligny, Chassagne and Bienvenues-Bâtard-Montrachet grand cru sit at the top.

fourrier.name: Domaine Fourrier
fourrier.line: A Gevrey estate famous for reds, also making a small Bourgogne Blanc.
fourrier.tell: Fourrier is a top Gevrey-Chambertin estate, best known for red. The Bourgogne Blanc is a small, fresh and pure white from a prized producer.

domaine-leflaive.name: Domaine Leflaive
domaine-leflaive.line: The great biodynamic estate of Puligny-Montrachet, with premier and grand cru vineyards.
domaine-leflaive.tell: Leflaive is the name for Puligny-Montrachet: pure, floral, long whites from biodynamic vines. Clavoillon, Pucelles, Folatières and Combettes are premier crus, with Bâtard, Bienvenues and Chevalier-Montrachet at the top. The Mâcon-Verzé, by the glass and by the bottle, is the gentle door into the house.

leflaive-associes.name: Leflaive & Associés
leflaive-associes.line: A side label of Domaine Leflaive, made by its team from partner growers' biodynamic vines.
leflaive-associes.tell: Leflaive & Associés is made by the Domaine Leflaive team from partner growers' grapes. The Auxey-Duresses is fresh and floral: Leflaive style at a gentler price.

meo-camuzet.name: Domaine Méo-Camuzet
meo-camuzet.line: A top Vosne estate, best known for reds; Clos Saint-Philibert is its white from the Hautes Côtes de Nuits.
meo-camuzet.tell: Méo-Camuzet is a top Vosne-Romanée estate. Clos Saint-Philibert is its white from the hills above Nuits, crisp and fresh, a rare white from a red wine name.

morey-coffinet.name: Domaine Morey-Coffinet
morey-coffinet.line: A family estate in Chassagne, organic and biodynamic in its farming.
morey-coffinet.tell: Morey-Coffinet is a family estate in Chassagne-Montrachet. En Remilly is a premier cru and Les Houillères a village site, with a Bâtard-Montrachet grand cru at the top and a Rully as the value bottle.

paul-pillot.name: Domaine Paul Pillot
paul-pillot.line: A four-generation family estate in Chassagne, run by Thierry Pillot, with a pure, taut style.
paul-pillot.tell: Paul Pillot is a family domaine, run by Thierry Pillot and his sister. The wines are crisp and precise. Cailleret and Clos Saint-Jean are premier crus; Le Charmois a Saint-Aubin premier cru; the Aligoté a value bottle.

thierry-pillot.name: Thierry Pillot
thierry-pillot.line: The small négoce label of Thierry Pillot of Domaine Paul Pillot, started in 2017.
thierry-pillot.tell: Thierry Pillot makes these from bought-in grapes alongside his family domaine. Les Castets is a Saint-Aubin premier cru, Les Poruzots a Meursault premier cru; there are grand crus too.

roulot.name: Domaine Roulot
roulot.line: Jean-Marc Roulot's Meursault estate, among the most sought-after for pure, precise whites.
roulot.tell: Roulot is one of Meursault's most sought-after estates, with lean, crisp, pure wines. Les Luchets is a village site, Charmes and Bouchères are premier crus, and even the Aligoté and Bourgogne are prized and scarce.

tollot-beaut.name: Domaine Tollot-Beaut
tollot-beaut.line: A family estate in Chorey known for reds and a fine Corton-Charlemagne.
tollot-beaut.tell: Tollot-Beaut is a family estate in Chorey-lès-Beaune, known for reds. Its Corton-Charlemagne is a grand cru white, and the Bourgogne Côte d'Or is the easy entry.

etienne-sauzet.name: Domaine Etienne Sauzet
etienne-sauzet.line: A leading Puligny estate making finely chiselled whites up to grand cru.
etienne-sauzet.tell: Sauzet is a top Puligny-Montrachet estate with finely chiselled whites. Les Combettes, Les Referts and La Garenne are premier crus and Le Montrachet is the summit; Jardin du Calvaire is a Hautes Côtes white.

francois-carillon.name: François Carillon
francois-carillon.line: François Carillon's own Puligny estate, made after the family domaine divided in 2010.
francois-carillon.tell: François Carillon makes pure, precise Puligny. Les Folatières is a premier cru; Les Enseignères a village site; Les Murgers des Dents de Chien a Saint-Aubin premier cru.

ramonet.name: Domaine Ramonet
ramonet.line: A legendary Chassagne estate with holdings up to Le Montrachet.
ramonet.tell: Ramonet is a great Chassagne-Montrachet name, rich and long-lived. Les Ruchottes and Caillerets are Chassagne premier crus, Champs-Canet a Puligny premier cru, and the Aligoté and Mâcon are rare value bottles.

jean-philippe-fichet.name: Jean-Philippe Fichet
jean-philippe-fichet.line: A Meursault grower making taut, mineral whites.
jean-philippe-fichet.tell: Fichet is a respected Meursault grower with taut, mineral whites. His Bourgogne and Rully are crisp value bottles with real Côte de Beaune style.

liger-belair.name: Liger-Belair
liger-belair.line: A family name in the Côte de Nuits shared by two separate estates.
liger-belair.tell: Two Burgundy estates carry the Liger-Belair name, so ask the sommelier which one made this Aligoté. Expect a crisp, lemony white, a fresh start to a meal.

marc-colin.name: Domaine Marc Colin et Fils
marc-colin.line: A family estate in Saint-Aubin with vines across Chassagne and Puligny.
marc-colin.tell: Marc Colin is a family estate based in Saint-Aubin with vines across Chassagne and Puligny. Les Castets is a Saint-Aubin premier cru, Les Champs Gain a Chassagne premier cru, Cuvée Margot and Cuvée Luce named village wines, and Bâtard-Montrachet the grand cru.

pierre-girardin.name: Pierre Girardin
pierre-girardin.line: A young Meursault-based négociant and grower making precise whites.
pierre-girardin.tell: Pierre Girardin is a young producer based in Meursault. Éclat de Calcaire is a Bourgogne Blanc, crisp and mineral, and the list spells the name Giardin.

raymond-dupont-fahn.name: Raymond Dupont-Fahn
raymond-dupont-fahn.line: A small Monthelie estate making vivid whites in Meursault and Bourgogne.
raymond-dupont-fahn.tell: Dupont-Fahn is a small estate near Meursault. Les Tillets is a Meursault village site and Chaumes des Perrières a Bourgogne from near the village: vivid and fresh.

sylvaine-alain-normand.name: Sylvaine et Alain Normand
sylvaine-alain-normand.line: A family estate in the Mâconnais making fresh Chardonnay.
sylvaine-alain-normand.tell: The Normands are a family estate in the Mâconnais in southern Burgundy. Their Bourgogne is fresh, gentle Chardonnay at a fair price.

matrot.name: Domaine Matrot
matrot.line: A traditional Meursault estate run by Thierry and Pascale Matrot's family.
matrot.tell: Matrot is a traditional Meursault estate. Charmes and Perrières are premier crus, and the half-bottle Bourgogne suits one or two guests.

dujac.name: Domaine Dujac
dujac.line: A great Morey-Saint-Denis estate, famous for reds, with fine whites too.
dujac.tell: Dujac is a great Morey-Saint-Denis estate, best known for reds. Monts Luisants is a rare white premier cru in Morey, and Les Combettes and Les Folatières are Puligny premier crus.

ponsot.name: Domaine Ponsot
ponsot.line: A famous Morey estate; its white Monts Luisants comes from very old Aligoté vines.
ponsot.tell: Ponsot is a great Morey-Saint-Denis name. Clos des Monts Luisants is a white premier cru made from old Aligoté vines, and Corton-Charlemagne and Montrachet are its grand crus.

laurent-ponsot.name: Laurent Ponsot
laurent-ponsot.line: Laurent Ponsot's own house, started after he left the family domaine.
laurent-ponsot.tell: Laurent Ponsot ran his family's domaine for years before starting his own house. Charmes is a Meursault premier cru and Cuvée du Pandorea a village Meursault.

vougeraie.name: Domaine de la Vougeraie
vougeraie.line: A biodynamic Côte de Nuits estate whose Le Clos Blanc de Vougeot is a rare white in red country.
vougeraie.tell: Vougeraie is a biodynamic estate in the Côte de Nuits. Le Clos Blanc de Vougeot is a rare white premier cru in red wine country, offered in magnum and double magnum, and there is a white Beaune too.

dugat-py.name: Domaine Bernard Dugat-Py
dugat-py.line: A famous Gevrey estate known for reds, with whites from Chassagne, Meursault and Corton-Charlemagne.
dugat-py.tell: Dugat-Py is a famous Gevrey-Chambertin estate known for reds. Its whites include a Chassagne Morgeot from very old vines, a Pernand premier cru, Meursault and Corton-Charlemagne: rich and concentrated.

deux-montille.name: Maison Deux Montille
deux-montille.line: A négoce of siblings from the de Montille family, focused on whites.
deux-montille.tell: Deux Montille is the white wine house of Étienne and Alix de Montille. Sous Frétille is a Pernand-Vergelesses premier cru, crisp, fine and good value.

chateau-de-chorey.name: Domaine du Château de Chorey
chateau-de-chorey.line: A family estate based in a château at Chorey-lès-Beaune.
chateau-de-chorey.tell: Château de Chorey is a family estate near Beaune. Les Combottes is a white Pernand-Vergelesses, fresh and good value from the Côte de Beaune.

delarche.name: Domaine Delarche
delarche.tell: Delarche is a family estate in Pernand-Vergelesses. Les Combettes is a white from the village, fresh and mineral, a value Côte de Beaune bottle.

jean-jacques-girard.name: Jean-Jacques Girard
jean-jacques-girard.line: A family estate in Savigny with vines in Pernand-Vergelesses.
jean-jacques-girard.tell: Jean-Jacques Girard is a family estate with vines in Pernand-Vergelesses. Les Belles Filles is a white village site, fresh and good value.

bouchard-pere-fils.name: Bouchard Père et Fils
bouchard-pere-fils.line: One of Burgundy's largest and oldest houses, based in Beaune.
bouchard-pere-fils.tell: Bouchard is one of Burgundy's largest and oldest houses, based in Beaune. Corton-Charlemagne is a grand cru white, and this one comes in magnum for a table to share.

follin-arbelet.name: Domaine Follin-Arbelet
follin-arbelet.tell: Follin-Arbelet is a small estate in Aloxe-Corton. Corton-Charlemagne is its grand cru white, powerful and mineral.

drc.name: Domaine de la Romanée-Conti
drc.line: The most famous estate in Burgundy; its whites are Le Montrachet and Corton-Charlemagne.
drc.tell: Domaine de la Romanée-Conti is Burgundy's most famous name. Its whites are Le Montrachet and Corton-Charlemagne, rare and very costly, so always involve the sommelier.

vincent-girardin.name: Domaine Vincent Girardin
vincent-girardin.line: A Meursault house making whites across the Côte de Beaune.
vincent-girardin.tell: Vincent Girardin makes whites across the Côte de Beaune. Corton-Charlemagne is a grand cru, Sous le Château a Saint-Romain, and the Puligny Vieilles Vignes comes from old vines.

pierre-meurgey.name: Pierre Meurgey
pierre-meurgey.line: A Burgundy native and part grower, part négociant, with partner growers across the Côte d'Or.
pierre-meurgey.tell: Pierre Meurgey works with partner growers across Burgundy. This bottle is a white Beaune premier cru: Chardonnay with ripe orchard fruit and a fresh finish, a good value step into the Côte de Beaune.

henri-gilles-buisson.name: Domaine Henri et Gilles Buisson
henri-gilles-buisson.line: A family estate in Saint-Romain, high in the hills of the Côte de Beaune.
henri-gilles-buisson.tell: Buisson is a family estate in Saint-Romain, high in the cool hills of the Côte de Beaune. La Perrière is a crisp, mineral white and good value.

antoine-jobard.name: Antoine Jobard
antoine-jobard.line: A Meursault estate whose wines are tight when young and slow to open.
antoine-jobard.tell: Antoine Jobard makes classic Meursault, tight when young and slow to open. Charmes is a premier cru; ask the sommelier about decanting.

comtes-lafon.name: Domaine des Comtes Lafon
comtes-lafon.line: A great Meursault estate, biodynamic, making rich and long-lived whites.
comtes-lafon.tell: Lafon is a great Meursault name, biodynamic, with rich and long-lived whites. Charmes is a premier cru and Clos de la Baronne a village site.

heritiers-comte-lafon.name: Les Héritiers du Comte Lafon
heritiers-comte-lafon.line: The Lafon family's Mâconnais estate, making bright Chardonnay.
heritiers-comte-lafon.tell: This is the Mâconnais estate of the Lafon family of Meursault. Milly-Lamartine is fresh and floral, Lafon style at a value price.

guy-bocard.name: Domaine Guy Bocard
guy-bocard.line: A family estate in Meursault devoted to white wine.
guy-bocard.tell: Guy Bocard is a Meursault family estate devoted to white wine. Genevrières is a premier cru and Limozin a village site next to the premier crus; the list spells it Brocard.

marquis-d-angerville.name: Domaine Marquis d'Angerville
marquis-d-angerville.line: A great Volnay estate; its white Meursault Santenots is a premier cru.
marquis-d-angerville.tell: D'Angerville is a great Volnay name, known for reds. Les Santenots is a white Meursault premier cru from the estate, elegant and fine.

genot-boulanger.name: Domaine Génot-Boulanger
genot-boulanger.line: A family estate with vines across the Côte de Beaune.
genot-boulanger.tell: Génot-Boulanger is a family estate across the Côte de Beaune. Les Bouchères is a Meursault premier cru, Clos du Cromin a Meursault village site and La Garenne a Puligny premier cru.

jean-marie-bouzereau.name: Domaine Jean-Marie Bouzereau
jean-marie-bouzereau.line: A Meursault estate from the Bouzereau family.
jean-marie-bouzereau.tell: Jean-Marie Bouzereau is a Meursault family estate. Poruzots is a premier cru and Les Narvaux a village site on the hill above.

joseph-voillot.name: Domaine Joseph Voillot
joseph-voillot.line: A family estate in Volnay with white Meursault.
joseph-voillot.tell: Voillot is a family estate in Volnay, known for reds. Les Cras is its white Meursault premier cru, fresh and fine.

marchand-tawse.name: Marchand-Tawse
marchand-tawse.line: A Nuits-Saint-Georges house making wines across Burgundy.
marchand-tawse.tell: Marchand-Tawse is a Nuits-Saint-Georges house making wines across Burgundy. Genevrières is a Meursault premier cru, here in double magnum, and the village Meursault comes in bottle and magnum.

bitouzet-prieur.name: Bitouzet-Prieur
bitouzet-prieur.line: A family estate in Volnay and Meursault.
bitouzet-prieur.tell: Bitouzet-Prieur is a family estate in Volnay and Meursault. Les Corbins is a Meursault village site, classic and nutty.

florent-garaudet.name: Domaine Florent Garaudet
florent-garaudet.line: A small estate in Monthelie making Meursault.
florent-garaudet.tell: Garaudet is a small estate based in Monthelie. This is a village Meursault from old vines, here in magnum for a table to share.

xavier-monnot.name: Xavier Monnot
xavier-monnot.line: A Meursault estate making taut whites.
xavier-monnot.tell: Xavier Monnot is a Meursault estate with taut whites. Le Limozin is a village site beside the premier crus.

hubert-lamy.name: Domaine Hubert Lamy
hubert-lamy.line: The leading Saint-Aubin estate, known for very densely planted vines and precise whites.
hubert-lamy.tell: Hubert Lamy is the star of Saint-Aubin, known for very densely planted vines. En Remilly and Derrière chez Édouard are premier crus and La Princée a village wine: precise and mineral.

larue.name: Domaine Larue
larue.tell: Larue is a family estate in Saint-Aubin. Les Murgers des Dents de Chien is a Saint-Aubin premier cru, crisp and mineral and good value against Puligny.

jean-claude-bachelet.name: Jean-Claude Bachelet
jean-claude-bachelet.tell: Bachelet is a family estate in Saint-Aubin. Les Champlots is a premier cru, crisp and mineral and good value against its famous neighbours.

alain-chavy.name: Domaine Alain Chavy
alain-chavy.line: A family estate in Puligny making classic whites.
alain-chavy.tell: Alain Chavy is a Puligny-Montrachet family estate. Champ Gain is a premier cru, and the village Puligny is floral and fine.

benoit-ente.name: Benoît Ente
benoit-ente.line: A small Puligny estate making precise whites.
benoit-ente.tell: Benoît Ente is a small Puligny-Montrachet estate. His village Puligny is crisp, floral and fine.

pascal-clement.name: Pascal Clément
pascal-clement.line: A Burgundy producer making Puligny and Chassagne.
pascal-clement.tell: Pascal Clément makes Puligny and Chassagne. La Maltroie is a Chassagne premier cru, and the village Puligny is floral and fresh.

michel-niellon.name: Domaine Michel Niellon
michel-niellon.tell: Niellon is a small, revered Chassagne-Montrachet estate. Les Vergers and Clos de la Truffière are premier crus and Chevalier-Montrachet the grand cru.

paul-pernot.name: Paul Pernot
paul-pernot.tell: Paul Pernot is a family estate in Puligny-Montrachet. Bienvenues-Bâtard-Montrachet is a grand cru, rich and floral.

blain-gagnard.name: Domaine Blain-Gagnard
blain-gagnard.tell: Blain-Gagnard is a Chassagne-Montrachet family estate. Cailleret, Clos Saint-Jean and La Boudriotte are premier crus, rich yet fresh.

philippe-colin.name: Philippe Colin
philippe-colin.line: A Chassagne estate, part of the Colin family.
philippe-colin.tell: Philippe Colin is part of the Colin family of Chassagne-Montrachet. Clos Saint-Jean and La Maltroie are premier crus, rich and nutty.

vincent-sophie-morey.name: Vincent et Sophie Morey
vincent-sophie-morey.tell: Vincent and Sophie Morey make Chassagne-Montrachet. Les Embrazées is a premier cru, here in magnum for a table to share.

bruno-clavelier.name: Domaine Bruno Clavelier
bruno-clavelier.line: A biodynamic Vosne estate, best known for reds.
bruno-clavelier.tell: Clavelier is a biodynamic Vosne-Romanée estate, best known for reds. Les Glapigny is a white from old vines, a rare find.

jean-marc-vincent.name: Domaine Jean-Marc Vincent
jean-marc-vincent.line: A small Santenay estate making taut whites.
jean-marc-vincent.tell: Jean-Marc Vincent is a small Santenay estate with taut whites. Les Vignes Denses comes from very closely planted vines.

prunier-bonheur.name: Domaine Prunier-Bonheur
prunier-bonheur.tell: Prunier-Bonheur is a family estate in Auxey-Duresses. Their white is crisp and fresh, good value from the Côte de Beaune.

robert-chevillon.name: Domaine Robert Chevillon
robert-chevillon.line: A great Nuits-Saint-Georges estate, famous for reds, with a rare white.
robert-chevillon.tell: Robert Chevillon is a top Nuits-Saint-Georges estate, famous for reds. Its white Nuits-Saint-Georges from old vines is unusual and rare.

maison-leroy.name: Maison Leroy
maison-leroy.line: The négoce of Lalou Bize-Leroy, one of Burgundy's most celebrated names.
maison-leroy.tell: Maison Leroy is the house of Lalou Bize-Leroy, one of Burgundy's most celebrated names. Its wines are rare and costly; this one is a white Savigny-lès-Beaune.

pierre-guillemot.name: Pierre Guillemot
pierre-guillemot.tell: Guillemot is a family estate in Savigny-lès-Beaune. Dessus les Golardes and Vieilles Vignes are whites, fresh and good value.

jaeger-defaix.name: Domaine Jaeger-Defaix
jaeger-defaix.line: An organic Rully estate run by Hélène Jaeger-Defaix, with premier cru vines.
jaeger-defaix.tell: Jaeger-Defaix farms organically in Rully, in the Côte Chalonnaise. Rabourcé is a premier cru, and the list prints the name as Defaix Frères.

francois-lumpp.name: Domaine François Lumpp
francois-lumpp.tell: François Lumpp is a leading Givry estate in the Côte Chalonnaise. Crausot is a white premier cru, fresh and good value.

jean-marc-boillot.name: Domaine Jean-Marc Boillot
jean-marc-boillot.line: A Pommard estate with whites from Puligny and Rully.
jean-marc-boillot.tell: Jean-Marc Boillot makes whites across Burgundy. Meix Cadot is a Rully premier cru, crisp and good value.

jean-marc-pillot.name: Domaine Jean-Marc Pillot
jean-marc-pillot.line: A Chassagne estate with vines in Montagny.
jean-marc-pillot.tell: Jean-Marc Pillot is a Chassagne-Montrachet estate. Les Bassets is a Montagny white, crisp and good value.

vignerons-de-buxy.name: Les Vignerons Réunis à Buxy
vignerons-de-buxy.line: The cooperative of Buxy, making Montagny.
vignerons-de-buxy.tell: This is the Buxy cooperative in the Côte Chalonnaise. The Montagny premier cru is crisp, fresh white Burgundy at a fair price.

carrette.name: Domaine Carrette
carrette.tell: Carrette is a family estate in Pouilly-Fuissé in southern Burgundy. Les Crays is a single site, here in magnum: ripe and round.

roc-des-boutires.name: Domaine du Roc des Boutires
roc-des-boutires.tell: This is Pouilly-Fuissé from southern Burgundy. En Bertilionne is a single site: ripe, round Chardonnay with a fresh finish.

eric-forest.name: Eric Forest
eric-forest.line: A small Pouilly-Fuissé grower in Vergisson.
eric-forest.tell: Eric Forest is a small grower in Pouilly-Fuissé. 24 Carats is a ripe, round Chardonnay with a fresh finish.

robert-denogent.name: Robert Denogent
robert-denogent.line: A family estate in Fuissé making old-vine Pouilly-Fuissé.
robert-denogent.tell: Denogent makes Pouilly-Fuissé in southern Burgundy. Cuvée Claude Denogent is from old vines: rich and long.

pierre-sparr.name: Pierre Sparr
pierre-sparr.line: A long-established Alsace house making Crémant and grand cru whites.
pierre-sparr.tell: Pierre Sparr is an old Alsace house. The Crémant rosé by the glass is Pinot Noir sparkling wine, fresh and fruity; Mambourg and Schoenenbourg are grand cru whites, fuller and more aromatic.

albert-boxler.name: Albert Boxler
albert-boxler.line: A small, revered estate in Niedermorschwihr, famed for grand cru Riesling from the Brand and Sommerberg.
albert-boxler.tell: Boxler is one of Alsace's most admired small estates. Brand and Sommerberg are grand crus, and the Rieslings are intense, dry and mineral. The Muscat and Edelzwicker blend are lighter, aromatic surprises.

justin-boxler.name: Domaine Justin Boxler
justin-boxler.line: A family estate in Niedermorschwihr with vines in the Sommerberg grand cru.
justin-boxler.tell: Justin Boxler is a family estate in Niedermorschwihr. Sommerberg is a steep granite grand cru, and the Riesling is crisp and stony.

ostertag.name: Domaine Ostertag
