ostertag.line: A biodynamic estate in Epfig known for site-driven wines and a thoughtful, modern touch.
ostertag.tell: Ostertag is a biodynamic family estate. Muenchberg is a grand cru; Fronholz, Zellberg and Pflanzer are single sites. The Pinot Gris and Gewürztraminer can carry some sweetness; ask the sommelier which are dry.

weinbach.name: Domaine Weinbach
weinbach.line: A celebrated family estate in Kaysersberg, around the walled Clos des Capucins, making rich, pure whites.
weinbach.tell: Weinbach is one of Alsace's great family estates. Clos des Capucins is the walled vineyard by the house; Schlossberg and Mambourg are grand crus; Cuvée Théo and Sainte Catherine are named cuvées. Aromatic and generous.

trimbach.name: Trimbach
trimbach.line: A historic Ribeauvillé house famous for dry, firm, long-lived Riesling, above all Clos Ste Hune.
trimbach.tell: Trimbach makes dry, firm Alsace whites. Clos Ste Hune is one of the world's great Rieslings, from a tiny plot; Cuvée Frédéric Emile is its other top Riesling; Vendanges Tardives means late harvest and is sweeter.

maurice-schoech.name: Maurice Schoech
maurice-schoech.line: A family estate in Ammerschwihr with grand cru vines in Kaefferkopf and nearby sites.
maurice-schoech.tell: Schoech is a family estate in Ammerschwihr. Kaefferkopf, Furstentum and Schlossberg are grand crus, and the wines are ripe and aromatic; ask the sommelier which carry sweetness.

marcel-deiss.name: Domaine Marcel Deiss
marcel-deiss.line: A Bergheim estate that champions blends of grapes grown together, named for the vineyard rather than the grape.
marcel-deiss.tell: Marcel Deiss names wines for places, not grapes, and blends varieties grown together. Mambourg is a grand cru; Engelgarten a single site. Rich, layered and unusual.

melanie-pfister.name: Mélanie Pfister
melanie-pfister.line: A family estate in northern Alsace, run by Mélanie Pfister.
melanie-pfister.tell: Mélanie Pfister runs her family estate in the north of Alsace. Macération is a skin-contact white, so it has more texture and colour than usual; ask the sommelier about the grape.

kuentz-bas.name: Kuentz-Bas
kuentz-bas.line: An old house in Husseren-les-Châteaux, below the three castles that give one of its wines its name.
kuentz-bas.tell: Kuentz-Bas is an old Alsace house. Geisberg is a grand cru Riesling, and Trois Châteaux is a Sylvaner named for the castles above the village.

meyer-fonne.name: Meyer-Fonné
meyer-fonne.line: A family estate in Katzenthal making precise grand cru Riesling.
meyer-fonne.tell: Meyer-Fonné is a family estate in Katzenthal. Kaefferkopf and Schoenenbourg are grand crus, and the Rieslings are dry and fine.

rolly-gassmann.name: Rolly Gassmann
rolly-gassmann.line: A Rorschwihr family estate known for ripe, often off-dry wines released with bottle age.
rolly-gassmann.tell: Rolly Gassmann is a family estate in Rorschwihr. Kappelweg is a single site, and their wines often keep some sweetness, so ask the sommelier before promising dry.

dirler-cade.name: Dirler-Cadé
dirler-cade.line: A biodynamic family estate in Bergholtz in southern Alsace.
dirler-cade.tell: Dirler-Cadé is a biodynamic family estate in southern Alsace. Edelzwicker is a traditional blend of Alsace grapes: aromatic, fresh and easy.

zind-humbrecht.name: Zind-Humbrecht
zind-humbrecht.line: A great biodynamic estate in Turckheim making rich, powerful whites.
zind-humbrecht.tell: Zind-Humbrecht is one of Alsace's leaders, with rich, powerful whites. Goldert is a grand cru, and this one is Muscat, aromatic and rich.

andre-perret.name: André Perret
andre-perret.line: A Chavanay family estate, a reference for Condrieu, including the steep Chéry hillside.
andre-perret.tell: André Perret is a leading name in Condrieu, pure Viognier. Chéry is a famous steep site; Clos Chanson another. Floral, apricot-scented and rich, wonderful with crab and spiced dishes.

christophe-billon.name: Domaine Christophe Billon
christophe-billon.line: A small northern Rhône estate making Condrieu.
christophe-billon.tell: This is Condrieu, Viognier from the northern Rhône. Les Matisses is floral and rich, with apricot and a silky texture.

clusel-roch.name: Domaine Clusel-Roch
clusel-roch.line: An organic family estate in Ampuis, known for Côte-Rôtie and Condrieu.
clusel-roch.tell: Clusel-Roch is an organic family estate in Ampuis. Verchery is a Condrieu site: floral, fresh and silky.

georges-vernay.name: Domaine Georges Vernay
georges-vernay.line: The great Condrieu estate, credited with keeping Viognier alive when the appellation was nearly lost.
georges-vernay.tell: Georges Vernay is the name in Condrieu, credited with saving the grape there. Les Terrasses de l'Empire is its classic Condrieu: apricot, flowers and a silky texture.

rene-rostaing.name: René Rostaing
rene-rostaing.line: An Ampuis estate famous for Côte-Rôtie, also making Condrieu.
rene-rostaing.tell: Rostaing is a famous Côte-Rôtie estate. La Bonnette is its Condrieu: floral, rich and silky.

tardieu-laurent.name: Tardieu-Laurent
tardieu-laurent.line: A Rhône négociant making rich wines from old vines.
tardieu-laurent.tell: Tardieu-Laurent buys from old vines across the Rhône. This Vieilles Vignes Condrieu is rich and aromatic, with apricot and flowers.

barruol-lynch.name: Barruol Lynch
barruol-lynch.line: A partnership of Louis Barruol of Château de Saint Cosme and importer Kermit Lynch.
barruol-lynch.tell: Barruol Lynch joins Louis Barruol of Saint Cosme with Kermit Lynch. La Pierrelle is a Hermitage blanc from old Marsanne: rich, floral and long. The list prints Barroul.

bernard-faurie.name: Bernard Faurie
bernard-faurie.line: A tiny, traditional grower in Hermitage and Saint-Joseph.
bernard-faurie.tell: Bernard Faurie is a small, old-school grower. His white Hermitage is rich and long, made in tiny amounts.

paul-jaboulet-aine.name: Paul Jaboulet Aîné
paul-jaboulet-aine.line: The Hermitage house behind La Chapelle; Chevalier de Sterimberg is its white Hermitage.
paul-jaboulet-aine.tell: Jaboulet is the Hermitage house of La Chapelle. Chevalier de Sterimberg is its white Hermitage, Marsanne-led, rich and honeyed, built to age.

jean-louis-chave.name: Domaine Jean-Louis Chave
jean-louis-chave.line: The great family estate of Hermitage, making red and white of legendary depth.
jean-louis-chave.tell: Chave is the greatest name on the hill of Hermitage. The white is Marsanne-led, rich, layered and very long-lived, a collector's bottle.

guigal.name: E. Guigal
guigal.line: The great Ampuis house; Ex Voto is its prestige Hermitage.
guigal.tell: Guigal is a giant of the Rhône. Ex Voto is its top white Hermitage: rich, oaky and powerful, for the grandest fish and white meat dishes.

domaine-de-la-charbonniere.name: Domaine de la Charbonnière
domaine-de-la-charbonniere.tell: La Charbonnière is a family estate in Châteauneuf-du-Pape. Its white is round, rich and gently floral.

domaine-de-nalys.name: Domaine de Nalys
domaine-de-nalys.line: A Châteauneuf-du-Pape estate making red and white.
domaine-de-nalys.tell: Nalys is a Châteauneuf-du-Pape estate. Its white is round, floral and rich, a southern white for spiced dishes.

alain-graillot.name: Alain Graillot
alain-graillot.line: The estate that set the standard for Crozes-Hermitage.
alain-graillot.tell: Graillot set the standard for Crozes-Hermitage. The white is fresh, floral and textured.

dard-ribo.name: Dard et Ribo
dard-ribo.tell: Dard et Ribo make low-intervention wines in Crozes-Hermitage. Their white is textured, fresh and a little wild.

auguste-clape.name: Auguste Clape
auguste-clape.line: The great Cornas estate; Saint-Péray is its white.
auguste-clape.tell: Clape is the reference estate of Cornas. Its Saint-Péray is a white from the neighbouring village: textured and fresh.

chateau-de-fonsalette.name: Château de Fonsalette
chateau-de-fonsalette.line: The Côtes du Rhône estate of the Reynaud family of Château Rayas.
chateau-de-fonsalette.tell: Fonsalette belongs to the family of Château Rayas. Its white Côtes du Rhône is rich and textured, far above the usual.

domaine-des-tours.name: Domaine des Tours
domaine-des-tours.line: An estate of Emmanuel Reynaud of Château Rayas.
domaine-des-tours.tell: Domaine des Tours is from the Reynaud family of Château Rayas. The Réserve white is round and aromatic.

sang-des-cailloux.name: Domaine Le Sang des Cailloux
sang-des-cailloux.tell: This is Vacqueyras in the southern Rhône. Un Sang Blanc is a white: round, aromatic and warm.

saint-damien.name: Domaine Saint Damien
saint-damien.tell: Saint Damien is a family estate in Gigondas. Les Prés is a white from Clairette: fresh and floral.

stephane-ogier.name: Stéphane Ogier
stephane-ogier.line: An Ampuis estate famous for Côte-Rôtie.
stephane-ogier.tell: Ogier is a Côte-Rôtie estate. Rosine is a Viognier from the hills nearby: floral, fresh and good value.

carbonnieux.name: Château Carbonnieux
carbonnieux.line: A classed growth of Graves in Pessac-Léognan, well known for its white.
carbonnieux.tell: Carbonnieux is a classed growth of Graves with a famous white of Sauvignon Blanc and Sémillon. It is crisp, citrusy and lightly oaked, lovely with fish and crab.

enclos-de-carbonnieux.name: L'Enclos de Carbonnieux
enclos-de-carbonnieux.line: A white Pessac-Léognan with the Carbonnieux name.
enclos-de-carbonnieux.tell: This is white Pessac-Léognan, Sauvignon Blanc and Sémillon, crisp and citrusy. Ask the sommelier how it relates to Château Carbonnieux.

couhins.name: Château Couhins
couhins.line: A classed growth of Graves in Pessac-Léognan, owned by France's national agricultural research institute.
couhins.tell: Couhins is a classed growth white of Pessac-Léognan. It is Sauvignon-led, crisp and citrusy, good with seafood.

chateau-guiraud.name: Château Guiraud
chateau-guiraud.line: A Sauternes first growth; G is its dry white.
chateau-guiraud.tell: Guiraud is a great Sauternes estate. G is its dry white, Sauvignon Blanc and Sémillon, crisp and lightly rich, a value Bordeaux white.

haut-brion.name: Château Haut-Brion
haut-brion.line: The first growth of Pessac-Léognan, whose white is among the rarest in Bordeaux.
haut-brion.tell: Haut-Brion is a first growth. Its white is Sémillon and Sauvignon Blanc, rich and long, made in small amounts and very costly, so involve the sommelier.

chateau-le-puy.name: Château Le Puy
chateau-le-puy.line: A biodynamic family estate on the Bordeaux plateau, long organic.
chateau-le-puy.tell: Le Puy is a family estate long farmed without chemicals. Marie-Cécile is its white, Sémillon: textured and gentle.

malartic-lagraviere.name: Château Malartic-Lagravière
malartic-lagraviere.line: A Graves classed growth in Pessac-Léognan.
malartic-lagraviere.tell: Malartic-Lagravière is a classed growth of Pessac-Léognan. The white is Sauvignon-led, crisp and fresh with gentle oak; ask the sommelier to confirm the estate, since the list prints Château Malartic Graves.

pape-clement.name: Château Pape Clément
pape-clement.tell: Pape Clément is an old classed growth of Pessac-Léognan. The white is rich, lightly oaked and long.

domaine-de-chevalier.name: Domaine de Chevalier
domaine-de-chevalier.line: A Graves classed growth whose white is one of Bordeaux's finest.
domaine-de-chevalier.tell: Domaine de Chevalier makes one of Bordeaux's finest whites. It is Sauvignon Blanc and Sémillon, precise and long.

domaine-de-l-alliance.name: Domaine de l'Alliance
domaine-de-l-alliance.tell: Domaine de l'Alliance is a small Bordeaux estate. Définition is a white; ask the sommelier about its grapes and style.

clos-cancaillau.name: Clos Cancaillau
clos-cancaillau.tell: This is Jurançon, from the foothills of the Pyrenees. Au Lavoir is a dry white, crisp and exotic.

domaine-labet.name: Domaine Labet
domaine-labet.line: A family estate in the Jura, known for single-site Chardonnay.
domaine-labet.tell: Labet is a family estate in the Jura. Les Varrons is a Chardonnay, crisp and mineral, topped up so it stays fresh.

rousset-martin.name: François Rousset-Martin
rousset-martin.line: A small Jura grower making Chardonnay and Savagnin.
rousset-martin.tell: Rousset-Martin is a small Jura grower. Terres Blanches is a Chardonnay and Clos Bacchus a Savagnin, both precise and savoury.

ganevat.name: Jean-François Ganevat
ganevat.line: A cult Jura grower making many tiny cuvées.
ganevat.tell: Ganevat is a cult name in the Jura. Les Varrons and Cuvée Marguerite are Chardonnays, precise and deep.

chateau-simone.name: Château Simone
chateau-simone.line: The estate that dominates the tiny Palette appellation near Aix.
chateau-simone.tell: Château Simone is almost all of Palette, a tiny appellation near Aix. Its white is textured, herbal and long-lived.

sylvain-morey.name: Sylvain Morey
sylvain-morey.line: A Burgundian making wine in the Luberon.
sylvain-morey.tell: Sylvain Morey comes from a Burgundy family and makes wine in the Luberon. Panorama is a white, fresh and round, and good value.

trevallon.name: Domaine de Trévallon
trevallon.line: A celebrated Provence estate in the Alpilles.
trevallon.tell: Trévallon is a celebrated estate in the Alpilles of Provence. Its white is rich and aromatic, and offered in several vintages.

tempier.name: Domaine Tempier
tempier.line: The great Bandol estate, famous for red and rosé.
tempier.tell: Tempier is the name in Bandol. Its rosé, Mourvèdre-led, is dry and savoury, a rosé for food rather than the pool.

boom-shucka.name: Boom Shucka
boom-shucka.line: A Chenin Blanc white from the Limoux area of the Languedoc.
boom-shucka.tell: Boom Shucka is a Chenin Blanc from the Limoux area of the Languedoc. Ask the sommelier about the producer before you tell its story.

grange-des-peres.name: Domaine de la Grange des Pères
grange-des-peres.line: A cult Languedoc estate making tiny amounts of red and white.
grange-des-peres.tell: Grange des Pères is a cult name in the Languedoc. Its white is rich and rare, made in tiny amounts.

hirsch.name: Weingut Hirsch
hirsch.line: A Kamptal family estate, organic and biodynamic, known for Heiligenstein Riesling and Grüner Veltliner.
hirsch.tell: Hirsch is an organic family estate in the Kamptal. Lamm is a Grüner Veltliner site, and Gaisberg and Heiligenstein are Riesling sites: crisp, mineral and precise.

laurenz-v.name: Laurenz V.
laurenz-v.tell: Laurenz V. specialises in Grüner Veltliner, Austria's signature white. Friendly is fresh, peppery and easy, a great value white.

loimer.name: Loimer
loimer.tell: Loimer is a biodynamic estate in the Kamptal. Lois is a fresh, peppery Grüner Veltliner, crisp and good value.

hermann-moser.name: Hermann Moser
hermann-moser.tell: Hermann Moser is a family estate in Kremstal. Gebling Hannah is a Grüner Veltliner Reserve, round and peppery, with some bottle age.

stadt-krems.name: Weingut Stadt Krems
stadt-krems.line: The winery owned by the town of Krems.
stadt-krems.tell: Stadt Krems is the winery owned by the town of Krems. The Classic Grüner Veltliner is crisp, peppery and good value.

emmerich-knoll.name: Emmerich Knoll
emmerich-knoll.tell: Knoll is a classic Wachau family estate. Kellerberg is a famous Riesling site, and this mature bottle is dry, rich and mineral.

franz-hirtzberger.name: Franz Hirtzberger
franz-hirtzberger.tell: Hirtzberger is a top Wachau name. Honivogl and Singerriedel are famous sites, and Smaragd is the ripest dry style: rich yet fresh.

frischengruber.name: Frischengruber
frischengruber.line: A family estate in the Wachau.
frischengruber.tell: Frischengruber is a family estate in the Wachau. Federspiel is a lighter dry style of Grüner Veltliner, crisp and peppery.

mathias-hirtzberger.name: Mathias Hirtzberger
mathias-hirtzberger.line: A Wachau grower from the Hirtzberger family.
mathias-hirtzberger.tell: Mathias Hirtzberger is from the Hirtzberger family of the Wachau. Ried Kollmitz is a Smaragd Riesling, the ripest dry style.

nikolaihof.name: Nikolaihof
nikolaihof.line: A historic biodynamic Wachau estate known for long-aged releases.
nikolaihof.tell: Nikolaihof is a historic biodynamic Wachau estate. Vinothek is a Riesling held many years in cask before release, so this old vintage is mature and complex.

veyder-malberg.name: Peter Veyder-Malberg
veyder-malberg.line: A small Wachau grower farming steep terraces.
veyder-malberg.tell: Veyder-Malberg farms steep terraces in the Wachau. Elsarner Brandstatt and Wachauer 2B are dry Rieslings, pure and mineral.

pichler-krutzler.name: Pichler-Krutzler
pichler-krutzler.tell: Pichler-Krutzler is a Wachau estate. In der Wand is a dry Riesling from a steep site, mineral and fine.

prager.name: Prager
prager.tell: Prager is a top Wachau name. Bodenstein is a high Grüner Veltliner site, dry, rich and mineral.

rudi-pichler.name: Rudi Pichler
rudi-pichler.tell: Rudi Pichler is a top Wachau name. Hochrain is a Smaragd Riesling, here with some bottle age.

gut-oggau.name: Gut Oggau
gut-oggau.line: A biodynamic Burgenland estate known for its painted family-portrait labels.
gut-oggau.tell: Gut Oggau is a biodynamic estate in Burgenland with painted family portraits on its labels. Weiss is a Grüner Veltliner blend, textured and natural in style.

kiralyudvar.name: Királyudvar
kiralyudvar.line: A Tokaj estate making dry and sweet Furmint.
kiralyudvar.tell: Királyudvar is a biodynamic Tokaj estate. This is a dry Furmint, crisp and a little smoky.

clemens-busch.name: Clemens Busch
clemens-busch.tell: Clemens Busch farms organically on the Mosel. Nonnengarten Trocken is a dry Riesling, mineral and fine.

dr-hermann.name: Dr. Hermann
dr-hermann.tell: Dr. Hermann is a family estate in Erden on the Mosel. The Spätlese and Auslese bottles are sweeter Rieslings, lovely with spice or dessert.

egon-muller.name: Egon Müller
egon-muller.line: The most famous estate of the Saar, owner of the Scharzhofberg.
egon-muller.tell: Egon Müller is the Saar's great name and the leading owner on the Scharzhofberg hill. The Kabinett is light and gently sweet, delicate and very rare.

fritz-haag.name: Fritz Haag
fritz-haag.tell: Fritz Haag is a top Mosel estate in Brauneberg. The Kabinett is light and gently sweet, here with some bottle age.

hermann-ludes.name: Hermann Ludes
hermann-ludes.tell: Hermann Ludes is a Mosel grower. Ask the sommelier how dry this Riesling is before you describe it.

jj-prum.name: Joh. Jos. Prüm
jj-prum.tell: JJ Prüm is a legendary Mosel name. Wehlener Sonnenuhr Kabinett is light and gently sweet, and it ages beautifully.

julian-haart.name: Julian Haart
julian-haart.tell: Julian Haart is a young Mosel grower. 1,000L Trocken is a dry Riesling, crisp and mineral.

max-ferd-richter.name: Max Ferd. Richter
max-ferd-richter.tell: Max Ferd. Richter is a family estate on the Mosel. Juffer-Sonnenuhr GG is a dry grand cru Riesling.

peter-lauer.name: Peter Lauer
peter-lauer.line: A Saar family estate that numbers each wine by its cask.
peter-lauer.tell: Lauer is a Saar family estate that names each wine by its cask, or Fass, number. Kern, Feils, Stirn and Neuenberg are sites, mostly dry or nearly so; ask the sommelier which carry sweetness.

schloss-lieser.name: Schloss Lieser
schloss-lieser.line: A Mosel estate run by Thomas Haag.
schloss-lieser.tell: Schloss Lieser is a top Mosel estate. Graacher Himmelreich Kabinett is light and gently sweet, and the list prints the name Leiser.

stein.name: Weingut Stein
stein.tell: Stein makes Mosel Riesling. Palmberg is a site; Trocken on the label means dry, Feinherb means off-dry.

weiser-kunstler.name: Weiser-Künstler
weiser-kunstler.tell: Weiser-Künstler is a small Mosel estate. Ellergrub is a steep slate site; ask the sommelier how dry it is.

georg-breuer.name: Georg Breuer
georg-breuer.line: A Rheingau estate known for dry Riesling.
georg-breuer.tell: Breuer is a Rheingau estate known for dry Riesling. Rauenthaler Nonnenberg is one of its sites, and the Trocken is dry, firm and fine.

jb-becker.name: J.B. Becker
jb-becker.line: A Walluf estate known for traditional, long-aged Riesling.
jb-becker.tell: Becker makes traditional Rheingau Riesling in Walluf, aged long before release. Walkenberg and Sonnenberg are sites; Trocken means dry, and the Spätlese without it is sweeter.

robert-weil.name: Robert Weil
robert-weil.line: A leading Rheingau estate in Kiedrich.
robert-weil.tell: Robert Weil is a top Rheingau estate in Kiedrich. The Kabinett is gently sweet, while the Trocken wines, Kiedricher and Monte Nostrum, are dry.

gunderloch.name: Gunderloch
gunderloch.tell: Gunderloch is a Rheinhessen estate in Nackenheim. Hipping GG is a dry grand cru Riesling from red slate soil.

keller.name: Keller
keller.tell: Keller is a cult name in Rheinhessen. Von der Fels is dry and Limestone Kabinett gently sweet, while Morstein and Hubacker GG are dry grand crus and very sought after.

donnhoff.name: Dönnhoff
donnhoff.tell: Dönnhoff is the Nahe's greatest name. Hermannshöhle and Brücke are famous sites; the GG is dry, while Spätlese and Auslese are sweeter.

emrich-schonleber.name: Emrich-Schönleber
emrich-schonleber.tell: Emrich-Schönleber is a top Nahe estate. Halgans Trocken is a dry Riesling, crisp and mineral.

schlossgut-diel.name: Schlossgut Diel
schlossgut-diel.tell: Diel is a Nahe estate. Burg Layer Trocken is a dry Riesling, crisp and fine.

hexamer.name: Hexamer
hexamer.tell: Hexamer is a Nahe family estate. Kabinett and Spätlese are sweeter, while the Trocken is dry.

kruger-rumpf.name: Kruger-Rumpf
kruger-rumpf.tell: Kruger-Rumpf is a Nahe family estate. Im Pitterberg GG is a dry grand cru Riesling, here in half-bottle.

burklin-wolf.name: Dr. Bürklin-Wolf
burklin-wolf.tell: Bürklin-Wolf is a large biodynamic Pfalz estate. R Wachenheim is a dry Riesling, here in magnum.

koehler-ruprecht.name: Koehler-Ruprecht
koehler-ruprecht.tell: Koehler-Ruprecht is a traditional Pfalz estate. Kallstadter Steinacker is a Riesling site, and there is a dry Pinot Blanc too.

lukas-hammelmann.name: Lukas Hammelmann
lukas-hammelmann.tell: Lukas Hammelmann is a Pfalz grower. Ask the sommelier about the grapes and how dry each wine is.

von-buhl.name: Reichsrat von Buhl
von-buhl.tell: Von Buhl is a historic Pfalz estate. Forster Jesuitengarten is a famous site, and this bottle has some age.

von-winning.name: Von Winning
von-winning.tell: Von Winning is a Pfalz estate. Kirchenstück and Ungeheuer are dry grand cru Rieslings, and Lime Rift is a Sauvignon Blanc.

lassak.name: Lassak
lassak.tell: Lassak is a Württemberg grower. This is a dry Riesling; ask the sommelier about its style.

moritz-kissinger.name: Moritz Kissinger
moritz-kissinger.tell: Moritz Kissinger is a Rheinhessen grower. 0 Ohm is a white blend of Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc.

knewitz.name: Weingut Knewitz
knewitz.tell: Knewitz is a family estate in Rheinhessen. This is a German Chardonnay, crisp and fine.

hans-wirsching.name: Hans Wirsching
hans-wirsching.line: A Franken estate known for Silvaner.
hans-wirsching.tell: Wirsching is a Franken estate known for Silvaner. The Trocken is dry and earthy, with some bottle age.

gaia.name: Gaia
gaia.line: A Greek estate making Assyrtiko on Santorini.
gaia.tell: Gaia makes Assyrtiko on the volcanic island of Santorini. Wild Ferment is crisp, saline and textured, superb with seafood.

grosjean.name: Grosjean
grosjean.line: A family estate in Valle d'Aosta.
grosjean.tell: Grosjean is a family estate in the alpine Valle d'Aosta. Petite Arvine is a mountain white, crisp and saline.

borgo-san-daniele.name: Borgo San Daniele
borgo-san-daniele.tell: Borgo San Daniele is a Friuli estate. Friulano is a round, almond-scented white, good with lighter dishes.

ca-marcanda.name: Ca' Marcanda
ca-marcanda.tell: Ca' Marcanda is the Gaja family's estate on the Tuscan coast. Vistamare is a white blend, fresh and aromatic.

cantina-terlano.name: Cantina Terlano
cantina-terlano.line: An Alto Adige cooperative known for long-lived whites.
cantina-terlano.tell: Terlano is an Alto Adige cooperative famous for long-lived whites. The Pinot Bianco and Winkl Sauvignon are crisp, and Nova Domus is a richer blend.

collecapretta.name: Collecapretta
collecapretta.tell: Collecapretta is a small family estate in Umbria. Trebbiano Spoletino from old vines is a textured, characterful white.

quintarelli.name: Giuseppe Quintarelli
quintarelli.tell: Quintarelli is a legend of Valpolicella. Ca' del Merlo is better known as a red, so ask the sommelier what this bottle is before you describe it.

la-capranera.name: La Capranera
la-capranera.tell: La Capranera is a Campania estate. Falanghina is a fresh, citrusy southern white and good value.

possa.name: Possa
possa.line: A small Cinque Terre grower on steep terraces.
possa.tell: Possa farms steep terraces in the Cinque Terre on the Ligurian coast. Triple A is a white; ask the sommelier about its grapes.

vignai-da-duline.name: Vignai da Duline
vignai-da-duline.tell: Vignai da Duline is a small Friuli estate. Giallado is a Tocai Giallo white, here in magnum.

vodopivec.name: Vodopivec
vodopivec.line: A Carso grower devoted to Vitovska.
vodopivec.tell: Vodopivec is devoted to Vitovska, a grape of the Carso near Trieste. This mature bottle is textured and savoury.

do-ferreiro.name: Do Ferreiro
do-ferreiro.line: A Rías Baixas estate known for old-vine Albariño.
do-ferreiro.tell: Do Ferreiro makes Albariño in Rías Baixas. Cepas Vellas comes from very old vines and has more depth than most.

lopez-de-heredia.name: López de Heredia
lopez-de-heredia.tell: López de Heredia is Rioja's great traditionalist house in Haro. Gravonia is an aged white, nutty and savoury, unlike any young white.

envinate.name: Envínate
envinate.line: A group of friends making wines in the Canaries.
envinate.tell: Envínate is a group of friends making wine in the Canary Islands. Listán Blanco grows there on volcanic soils, giving crisp, salty, smoky whites.

familia-torres.name: Familia Torres
familia-torres.tell: Torres is the great Catalan wine family. Forcada is a white from an old local grape the family brought back.

granbazan.name: Granbazán
granbazan.tell: Granbazán is a Rías Baixas estate. Don Álvaro is an Albariño, crisp and citrusy.

raul-perez.name: Raúl Pérez
raul-perez.tell: Raúl Pérez is an influential winemaker in Bierzo. Ultreia is a Godello white, textured and mineral.

terroir-al-limit.name: Terroir al Límit
terroir-al-limit.tell: Terroir al Límit is a Priorat estate. Historic White is a Muscat of Alexandria, aromatic and dry in style; ask the sommelier to confirm.

ashanta.name: Ashanta
ashanta.line: A small natural-wine label founded by Chenoa Ashton-Lewis and Will Basanta, working with organic vineyards.
ashanta.tell: Ashanta is a small natural-wine label from a young California couple. Calypso is a Chardonnay made with nothing added or taken away, so it is crisp, zesty and mineral, far from buttery California. A good talking point for an adventurous guest.

chalk-hill.name: Chalk Hill
chalk-hill.line: A Sonoma estate in its own small appellation, known for rich Chardonnay.
chalk-hill.tell: Chalk Hill is a Sonoma estate known for Chardonnay. Expect a round, ripe style with toasty oak. Here in half-bottle, right for one or two guests.

del-dotto.name: Del Dotto
del-dotto.line: A Napa family winery known for its wine caves, also bottling Sonoma Coast Chardonnay.
del-dotto.tell: Del Dotto is a Napa family winery famous for its caves. This Chardonnay comes from Fort Ross-Seaview, a cool, high corner of the Sonoma Coast, so it has freshness under its ripe fruit.

fisher.name: Fisher Vineyards
fisher.line: A family estate high in the Mayacamas mountains on the Sonoma side.
fisher.tell: Fisher is a family winery on the mountain ridge between Sonoma and Napa. Mountain Estate Chardonnay is concentrated and balanced, and this bottle has some age.

hirsch-vineyards.name: Hirsch Vineyards
hirsch-vineyards.line: A pioneering vineyard on the far Sonoma Coast, near the ocean, known for taut Pinot Noir and Chardonnay.
hirsch-vineyards.tell: Hirsch Vineyards sits on a ridge near the Pacific on the far Sonoma Coast. The Estate Chardonnay is lean, bright and mineral, closer to Burgundy than to classic California.

kalin-cellars.name: Kalin Cellars
kalin-cellars.line: A small California winery known for releasing its wines only after long ageing.
kalin-cellars.tell: Kalin Cellars holds its wines for years before release, so a Kalin bottle arrives with mature, layered flavours. Cuvée CH is a Sonoma Coast Chardonnay; ask the sommelier about the vintage.

kistler.name: Kistler
kistler.line: A Sonoma specialist in Chardonnay and Pinot Noir, famous for rich, Burgundian single vineyard wines.
kistler.tell: Kistler is one of California's great Chardonnay names. Les Noisetiers is its Sonoma Coast blend: rich, creamy and fine, with real tension.

lioco.name: Lioco
lioco.line: A Sonoma winery making fresh, restrained Chardonnay and Pinot Noir.
lioco.tell: Lioco makes restrained California wines. Estero is a Russian River Valley Chardonnay, bright and citrusy rather than buttery, very good with seafood.

ramey.name: Ramey Wine Cellars
ramey.line: David Ramey's Sonoma winery, known for Burgundian-style single vineyard Chardonnay.
ramey.tell: Ramey is a leading Sonoma Chardonnay house. Rochioli Vineyard is a famous Russian River site, and the wine is rich, creamy and layered.

stonestreet.name: Stonestreet
stonestreet.line: A Jackson Family estate on mountain slopes above the Alexander Valley.
stonestreet.tell: Stonestreet farms high mountain vineyards above the Alexander Valley. Estate Vineyard and Upper Barn Chardonnays are ripe and powerful, with the freshness of altitude.

vokel.name: Vokel Cellars
vokel.line: A small producer of Chardonnay and Pinot Noir.
vokel.tell: Vokel Cellars is a small producer focused on Chardonnay and Pinot Noir. Heintz Vineyard is a well-known Sonoma Coast site. Ask the sommelier about the style before you describe it.

brick-and-mortar.name: Brick & Mortar
brick-and-mortar.line: A small California producer; Cougar Rock is a Napa Valley Chardonnay.
brick-and-mortar.tell: Brick & Mortar is a small California producer. Cougar Rock is a Napa Valley Chardonnay; ask the sommelier about its style before you describe it.

cakebread.name: Cakebread Cellars
cakebread.line: A Rutherford family winery whose Napa Chardonnay is a long-time restaurant favourite.
cakebread.tell: Cakebread is a family winery in Rutherford. The Chardonnay is a classic Napa style, ripe fruit, gentle oak and a fresh finish, and many guests know and ask for it.

chateau-montelena.name: Chateau Montelena
chateau-montelena.line: The Calistoga estate whose Chardonnay won the 1976 Paris tasting against white Burgundy.
chateau-montelena.tell: Montelena's Chardonnay famously beat top white Burgundies in the 1976 Paris tasting. It is still made in a restrained style, crisp and balanced, with little obvious oak.

far-niente.name: Far Niente
far-niente.line: An Oakville estate that makes only Chardonnay and Cabernet Sauvignon.
far-niente.tell: Far Niente is an Oakville estate that makes just Chardonnay and Cabernet. The Chardonnay is rich and creamy, with polished oak, here in magnum for a larger table.

forman.name: Forman
forman.line: Ric Forman's small Napa winery, making restrained Chardonnay and Cabernet.
forman.tell: Forman is Ric Forman's small Napa winery. The Chardonnay is lean and crisp for Napa, made without the buttery style.

frogs-leap.name: Frog's Leap
frogs-leap.line: A Rutherford winery known for organic, dry-farmed vineyards and balanced wines.
frogs-leap.tell: Frog's Leap farms organically in Rutherford without irrigation. Its Chardonnay and Sauvignon Blanc are fresh and balanced, crowd-pleasers with a story.

hyde-de-villaine.name: Hyde de Villaine
hyde-de-villaine.line: A partnership of the Hyde vineyard family and Aubert de Villaine of Burgundy.
hyde-de-villaine.tell: Hyde de Villaine joins the Hyde family's Carneros vineyard with Aubert de Villaine of Burgundy. The Chardonnay is elegant and mineral, California fruit with Burgundy restraint.

kongsgaard.name: Kongsgaard
kongsgaard.line: A small Napa winery famed for rich, long-aged Chardonnay; The Judge is its rarest.
kongsgaard.tell: Kongsgaard makes some of Napa's most sought-after Chardonnay: rich, deep and long. The Judge is the rare top bottling, a collector's white.

mayacamas.name: Mayacamas
mayacamas.line: A historic mountain estate on Mount Veeder, known for restrained, long-lived wines.
mayacamas.tell: Mayacamas is an old mountain estate high on Mount Veeder. The Chardonnay is lean and fresh, made without heavy oak, and it ages beautifully.

shafer.name: Shafer Vineyards
shafer.line: A Napa family winery; Red Shoulder Ranch is its Carneros Chardonnay.
shafer.tell: Shafer is a famous Napa family winery. Red Shoulder Ranch is its Chardonnay from cool Carneros: rich and creamy, with fresh acidity.

stony-hill.name: Stony Hill
stony-hill.line: A historic Spring Mountain estate known for lean, long-lived Chardonnay.
stony-hill.tell: Stony Hill is a historic estate on Spring Mountain. Its Chardonnay is lean and crisp, made without new oak, and it ages for years.

stout.name: Stout Family Wines
stout.tell: Stout is a small Napa family producer. The Carneros Chardonnay and Granny Rae's Sauvignon Blanc are offered; ask the sommelier about their style.

au-bon-climat.name: Au Bon Climat
au-bon-climat.line: Jim Clendenen's Santa Maria winery, a pioneer of Burgundian-style Chardonnay and Pinot Noir.
au-bon-climat.tell: Au Bon Climat helped put Santa Barbara on the map. The Chardonnays are balanced and fresh, and Hildegard is a richer white blend, including a mature 2002 in magnum.

calera.name: Calera
calera.line: Josh Jensen's estate on the limestone of Mount Harlan, planted to Burgundy grapes.
calera.tell: Calera chose Mount Harlan for its limestone, the soil of Burgundy. The Chardonnay is fresh and mineral, with real finesse.

clos-la-chance.name: Clos la Chance
clos-la-chance.tell: Clos la Chance is a Central Coast winery. This Monterey Chardonnay is an older vintage, so ask the sommelier how it is drinking.

lompoc-wine-co.name: Lompoc Wine Co.
lompoc-wine-co.tell: Lompoc Wine Company is a small label from the cool, windy Sta. Rita Hills in Santa Barbara County. This older Chardonnay should show some bottle age, so ask the sommelier how it is drinking before you promise freshness.

morgan.name: Morgan
morgan.tell: Morgan is a Santa Lucia Highlands winery. Rosella's is a famous vineyard, and this older Chardonnay should show bottle age; ask the sommelier how it is drinking.

presquile.name: Presqu'ile
presquile.line: A family winery in Santa Maria.
presquile.tell: Presqu'ile is a family winery in the Santa Maria Valley. Bien Nacido Vineyard Chardonnay is fresh and fine, and their rosé is light and dry.

sandhi.name: Sandhi
sandhi.line: A Sta. Rita Hills winery making lean, mineral Chardonnay.
sandhi.tell: Sandhi makes taut, mineral Chardonnay in the Sta. Rita Hills. Sanford & Benedict and La Rinconada are famous vineyards, and the Central Coast bottling is the value entry.

the-hilt.name: The Hilt
the-hilt.tell: The Hilt makes Chardonnay in the cool Sta. Rita Hills. Bentrock is a single vineyard by the ocean wind, fresh and fine.

the-paring.name: The Paring
the-paring.tell: The Paring is a Santa Barbara label. This Chardonnay is fresh and fruity, an easy, good-value white.

wind-gap.name: Wind Gap
wind-gap.tell: Wind Gap is a California winery. Yuen is a Chardonnay, here from an older vintage, so ask the sommelier how it is drinking.

beaux-freres.name: Beaux Frères
beaux-freres.tell: Beaux Frères is a Willamette Valley estate best known for Pinot Noir. This is its Chardonnay, fresh and fine.

bethel-heights.name: Bethel Heights
bethel-heights.line: A family estate in the Eola-Amity Hills.
bethel-heights.tell: Bethel Heights is a family estate in the Eola-Amity Hills. The Estate Chardonnay is fresh and bright, cool-climate Oregon at its best.

domaine-serene.name: Domaine Serene
domaine-serene.tell: Domaine Serene is a Dundee Hills estate. Evenstad Reserve is its top Chardonnay, rich yet fresh.

evening-land.name: Evening Land
evening-land.line: An Eola-Amity Hills estate around Seven Springs vineyard.
evening-land.tell: Evening Land farms Seven Springs vineyard in the Eola-Amity Hills. La Source and Summum are its top Chardonnays, taut and mineral.

eyrie.name: The Eyrie Vineyards
eyrie.tell: Eyrie pioneered wine in the Willamette Valley. These are mature Chardonnays from the 1980s and 1990s, rare library bottles to discuss with the sommelier.

martin-woods.name: Martin Woods
martin-woods.tell: Martin Woods is a small Oregon winery. Its single vineyard Chardonnays are fresh and precise.

penner-ash.name: Penner-Ash
penner-ash.tell: Penner-Ash is a Willamette Valley winery. Its Chardonnay and Viognier are offered, fresh and fruity.

roco.name: Roco
roco.tell: Roco is a Willamette Valley winery. Gravel Road is a Chardonnay, fresh and bright.

sixto.name: Sixto
sixto.tell: Sixto is a Washington Chardonnay label. Moxee is a vineyard, and this bottle has some age.

arkenstone.name: Arkenstone
arkenstone.tell: Arkenstone is a Howell Mountain estate in Napa. Its Sauvignon Blanc is rich and textured, a serious white.

bedrock.name: Bedrock Wine Co.
bedrock.line: A Sonoma winery known for old vineyards.
bedrock.tell: Bedrock is a Sonoma winery known for old vineyards. Its Sauvignon Blanc is fresh and textured.

capture.name: Capture
capture.tell: Capture is a mountain winery in northern Sonoma. Its Sauvignon Blanc is crisp and bright.

duckhorn.name: Duckhorn
duckhorn.tell: Duckhorn is a famous Napa name. Its Sauvignon Blanc is crisp and citrusy, and the half-bottle suits one or two.

jonata.name: Jonata
jonata.tell: Jonata is a Ballard Canyon estate in Santa Barbara County. Flor is its Sauvignon Blanc, rich and textured.

justin.name: Justin
justin.tell: Justin is a Paso Robles winery. Its Sauvignon Blanc is bright and fruity, good value.

kivelstadt.name: Kivelstadt Cellars
kivelstadt.tell: Kivelstadt is a Sonoma winery. The Family Secret is a Sauvignon Blanc, fresh and good value.

lieu-dit.name: Lieu Dit
lieu-dit.line: A Santa Barbara winery focused on Loire grapes.
lieu-dit.tell: Lieu Dit is a Santa Barbara winery focused on Loire grapes. Its Sauvignon Blanc is crisp and mineral.

long-meadow-ranch.name: Long Meadow Ranch
long-meadow-ranch.tell: Long Meadow Ranch is a Napa farm estate. Its Sauvignon Blanc is crisp and fresh.

miner.name: Miner Family Vineyards
miner.tell: Miner is a Napa family winery. Its Sauvignon Blanc is crisp and bright.

robert-mondavi.name: Robert Mondavi
robert-mondavi.line: The Napa winery that shaped modern California wine.
robert-mondavi.tell: Mondavi helped shape modern Napa. Its Sauvignon Blanc is crisp and lightly rich, a classic.

monte-rio.name: Monte Rio Cellars
monte-rio.tell: Monte Rio is a small California label. Its Lodi Sauvignon Blanc is fresh and easy.

st-supery.name: St. Supéry
st-supery.tell: St. Supéry is a Napa estate. Dollarhide is its ranch, and the Sauvignon Blanc is crisp and citrusy.

patricia-green.name: Patricia Green Cellars
patricia-green.tell: Patricia Green is an Oregon winery best known for Pinot Noir. Its Sauvignon Blanc is crisp and fresh.

alexana.name: Alexana
alexana.tell: Alexana is an Oregon winery. Hillsides is a fresh white; ask the sommelier about its grapes.

darioush.name: Darioush
darioush.tell: Darioush is a Napa estate. Its Viognier is rich, floral and peachy.

forge-cellars.name: Forge Cellars
forge-cellars.line: A Seneca Lake winery co-founded by Louis Barruol of Saint Cosme.
forge-cellars.tell: Forge Cellars is a Finger Lakes winery on Seneca Lake. Les Alliés is a dry Riesling, crisp and mineral.

forlorn-hope.name: Forlorn Hope
forlorn-hope.tell: Forlorn Hope works with unusual grapes in California. Rorick Vineyard is in the Sierra Foothills, and the Picpoul is crisp and saline.

dr-konstantin-frank.name: Dr. Konstantin Frank
dr-konstantin-frank.tell: Konstantin Frank pioneered European grapes in the Finger Lakes. The Dry Riesling is crisp and good value.

matthiasson.name: Matthiasson
matthiasson.tell: Matthiasson is a Napa winery known for unusual grapes. Ribolla Gialla is a textured white, here in older vintages.

pride-mountain.name: Pride Mountain Vineyards
pride-mountain.line: A mountain estate straddling Napa and Sonoma.
pride-mountain.tell: Pride Mountain straddles the Napa and Sonoma line high on Spring Mountain. Its Viognier is rich and floral.

ridge.name: Ridge Vineyards
ridge.tell: Ridge is a historic California winery. Its Grenache Blanc from Paso Robles is round and fresh.

teutonic.name: Teutonic Wine Co.
teutonic.line: An Oregon winery inspired by German wines.
teutonic.tell: Teutonic is an Oregon winery inspired by German wines. Candied Mushroom is a Riesling; ask the sommelier how dry it is.

willamette-valley-vineyards.name: Willamette Valley Vineyards
willamette-valley-vineyards.tell: Willamette Valley Vineyards is an Oregon winery. Its Pinot Gris is fresh and fruity, good value.

catena-zapata.name: Catena Zapata
catena-zapata.line: The Mendoza family house that led Argentina's move to high-altitude vineyards.
catena-zapata.tell: Catena Zapata led Argentina to high-altitude vineyards. White Stones is a Chardonnay from the Adrianna Vineyard, mineral and long.

bodega-chacra.name: Bodega Chacra
bodega-chacra.line: A Patagonian estate in Río Negro.
bodega-chacra.tell: Chacra is a Patagonian estate in Río Negro. Mainqué is its Chardonnay, fresh and precise.

el-enemigo.name: El Enemigo
el-enemigo.line: A Mendoza project of Alejandro Vigil and Adrianna Catena.
el-enemigo.tell: El Enemigo is a Mendoza project of Alejandro Vigil and Adrianna Catena. Its Chardonnay is fresh and good value.

bindi.name: Bindi
bindi.tell: Bindi is a small estate in Victoria's Macedon Ranges. Kostas Rind is a Chardonnay, fine and taut, with some age.

by-farr.name: By Farr
by-farr.tell: By Farr is a Geelong family estate. Its Chardonnay and Viognier are rich and fine.

giaconda.name: Giaconda
giaconda.line: A Beechworth estate famed for Chardonnay.
giaconda.tell: Giaconda is a Beechworth estate famed for Chardonnay. It is rich, complex and rare, among Australia's most sought-after whites.

seppeltsfield.name: Seppeltsfield
seppeltsfield.region: Barossa and Clare Valley, South Australia
seppeltsfield.tell: Seppeltsfield is a historic South Australian house. Watervale Riesling from the Clare Valley is dry, crisp and limey.

stargazer.name: Stargazer
stargazer.tell: Stargazer is a small Tasmanian estate. Palisander is a Riesling, crisp and fine.

tyrrells.name: Tyrrell's Wines
tyrrells.line: A Hunter Valley family house famous for Semillon.
tyrrells.tell: Tyrrell's is a Hunter Valley family house famous for Semillon. Vat 1 is light, lemony and ages for decades.

tara.name: Tara
tara.line: A Chilean project in the Atacama desert.
tara.tell: Tara comes from the Atacama desert in Chile. Its Chardonnay is crisp and saline, an unusual find.

kumeu-river.name: Kumeu River
kumeu-river.line: A family estate near Auckland famous for Chardonnay.
kumeu-river.tell: Kumeu River is a family estate near Auckland famous for Chardonnay. Coddington and Estate are fine and taut, and Kumeu Village is the value bottling.

badenhorst.name: A.A. Badenhorst
badenhorst.tell: Badenhorst is a Swartland family estate. Klip Klop is a Chenin Blanc, and the Palomino is an unusual, textured white.

capensis.name: Capensis
capensis.tell: Capensis is a South African Chardonnay project. The Western Cape Chardonnays are rich and fine, and Silene is its Stellenbosch bottling.

mullineux.name: Mullineux
mullineux.tell: Mullineux is a Swartland estate. Old Vines White is a Chenin Blanc-led blend, textured and good value.

quinta-essentia.name: Quinta Essentia
quinta-essentia.line: A Stellenbosch old-vine Chenin Blanc project.
quinta-essentia.tell: Quinta Essentia is an old-vine Chenin Blanc project in Stellenbosch. It is rich, textured and good value.

sadie.name: Sadie Family Wines
sadie.tell: Sadie is a Swartland leader. Palladius is a rich white blend, and Skurfberg and Rotsbank are old-vine Chenin Blancs.

spioenkop.name: Spioenkop
spioenkop.tell: Spioenkop is an Elgin estate. Its Chenin Blanc is crisp and mineral, here with some age.

chateau-d-esclans.name: Château d'Esclans
chateau-d-esclans.line: Sacha Lichine's Provence estate, maker of Whispering Angel.
chateau-d-esclans.tell: Whispering Angel is the famous pale Provence rosé from Château d'Esclans. It is dry, crisp and delicate, a guest favourite.

mesclances.name: Château les Mesclances
mesclances.tell: Mesclances is a Provence estate. Romane is a pale, dry rosé, crisp and good value.

gavoty.name: Domaine Gavoty
gavoty.tell: Gavoty is a Provence family estate. La Cigale is a pale, dry rosé, crisp and good value.

mas-de-valeriole.name: Mas de Valériole
mas-de-valeriole.tell: Valériole is an estate in the Camargue. Vé is a pale, dry rosé, offered in bottle and magnum.

bisson.name: Bisson
bisson.tell: Bisson is a Ligurian estate. This rosé is from Ciliegiolo, a red grape, fresh and fruity.

bon-ve.name: Bon Vé
bon-ve.line: A rosé the list files under the United States.
bon-ve.tell: The list files Bon Vé under the United States and names Georgia. Ask the sommelier about the producer and style before you describe it.

By the Glass.title: By the glass
By the Glass.line: Fourteen wines poured by the glass, priced per glass: sparkling, white, rosé and red, two of them through Coravin. Ask what the guest usually drinks and how hungry they are, then offer one choice and one step up.

By the Glass ~ Sparkling.title: Sparkling by the glass
By the Glass ~ Sparkling.line: Four bubbles: Brennan's Essential Champagne, an Oregon Brut, an Alsace Crémant rosé and Rare 2012 through Coravin. Ask whether it is a celebration; Rare is the splurge glass, Argyle the gentlest price.

By the Glass ~ White.title: White by the glass
By the Glass ~ White.line: Five whites from crisp to rich: Mosel Riesling, Albariño and Loire Sauvignon on the fresh side, California Chardonnay and Leflaive's Mâcon-Verzé through Coravin on the rounder side. Ask crisp or creamy first.

By the Glass ~ Rosé.title: Rosé by the glass
By the Glass ~ Rosé.line: One rosé, Minuty Prestige from Provence: pale, dry and delicate. Offer it to the guest who wants something light that still stands up to Creole flavours.

By the Glass ~ Red.title: Red by the glass
By the Glass ~ Red.line: Four reds from light to bold: Bourgogne Pinot Noir, a southern Rhône Grenache, a Bordeaux Supérieur and Inglenook Rubicon. Ask light or full; Rubicon is the splurge glass for steak.

Champagne.title: Champagne
Champagne.line: The deepest part of the list: famous houses and grower Champagnes, from about $50 to rare large formats. Ask the occasion, the budget and whether the guest likes crisp and light or rich and toasty.

Champagne ~ Grower Producers ~ Montagne.title: Growers: Montagne de Reims
Champagne ~ Grower Producers ~ Montagne.line: Family growers from the Pinot Noir villages around Reims, such as Bouzy and Ambonnay: fuller, red-fruited Champagne with body. Steer the guest who likes rich bubbles here, or toward Blanc de Noirs for food.

Champagne ~ Grower Producers ~ Vallée de.title: Growers: Vallée de la Marne
Champagne ~ Grower Producers ~ Vallée de.line: Growers along the Marne river, where Meunier and Pinot Noir dominate: fruity, generous, food-friendly Champagne, often good value. Ask whether the guest wants something round and easy or a single parcel to explore.

Champagne ~ Grower Producers ~ Côtes de.title: Growers: Côte des Blancs
Champagne ~ Grower Producers ~ Côtes de.line: Chardonnay country south of Épernay: Le Mesnil, Avize, Cramant, Vertus. Expect crisp, chalky, elegant Blanc de Blancs, superb with oysters and seafood. Selosse and Agrapart are the cult names; ask the budget first.

Champagne ~ Grower Producers ~ Aube.title: Growers: Aube
Champagne ~ Grower Producers ~ Aube.line: The Côte des Bar in the south of Champagne, Pinot Noir country closer to Burgundy than Reims. Ripe, fruit-driven wines, often low in dosage. A good corner for a curious guest at a gentler price.

Champagne ~ Grande Marques.title: The great houses
Champagne ~ Grande Marques.line: The famous names, from Piper-Heidsieck and Veuve Clicquot to Krug, Cristal, Dom Pérignon and Salon, plus magnums and giant bottles. Ask the budget and the occasion; most guests who name a brand want that brand.

International ~ Sparkling.title: Sparkling beyond Champagne
International ~ Sparkling.line: Traditional method bubbles from England, Austria, Italy, Portugal, Tasmania, the Jura and the United States, mostly under $250. Offer it to the guest who wants quality bubbles without Champagne prices, or something new.

International ~ Sparkling ~ Australia.title: Australian sparkling
International ~ Sparkling ~ Australia.line: One Tasmanian bottle, Jansz: cool-climate sparkling made the Champagne way, fresh and creamy at a friendly price.

International ~ Sparkling ~ Austria.title: Austrian sparkling
International ~ Sparkling ~ Austria.line: Bründlmayer and Schloss Gobelsburg, two great Kamptal estates, making serious traditional method sparkling wine, two of them in magnum. A strong pick for a Champagne lover open to a surprise.

International ~ Sparkling ~ England.title: English sparkling
International ~ Sparkling ~ England.line: Three bottles from Ridgeview in Sussex, where chalk soils echo Champagne. Crisp and lively, all under $100; a fun talking point for a curious guest.

International ~ Sparkling ~ Portugal.title: Portuguese sparkling
International ~ Sparkling ~ Portugal.line: Two magnums from Luis Pato in Bairrada, sparkling wines from local grapes. Good for a table of four or more who want something unusual.

International ~ Sparkling ~ France.title: French sparkling outside Champagne
International ~ Sparkling ~ France.line: One bottle from the Jura, Domaine du Pélican, the d'Angerville family's estate. A sparkling wine for a guest who likes Burgundy and wants something outside Champagne.

International ~ Sparkling ~ Italy.title: Italian sparkling
International ~ Sparkling ~ Italy.line: Franciacorta from Ca' del Bosco, Trento from Ferrari, and a cloudy col fondo from the Veneto. Ask whether the guest wants classic and polished or rustic and dry.

International ~ Sparkling ~ United State.title: American sparkling
International ~ Sparkling ~ United State.line: Oregon and California bubbles from Argyle, Domaine Carneros, Roederer Estate, Schramsberg and others, $70 to $255. A natural pick for a guest who loves Champagne houses and wants their American cousins.

France ~ Loire ~ White.title: Loire whites
France ~ Loire ~ White.line: Chenin Blanc, Sauvignon Blanc and Muscadet from France's longest river: mostly crisp, from about $50, with rare Savennières and Clos Rougeard at the top. Ask how dry the guest likes it; some Vouvray is sweet.

France ~ Loire ~ White ~ Muscadet Sèvre-.title: Muscadet
France ~ Loire ~ White ~ Muscadet Sèvre-.line: Crisp, saline whites from Melon de Bourgogne near the Atlantic, the classic match for raw oysters. These are serious, lees-aged Muscadets from top growers, $70 to $150.

France ~ Loire ~ White ~ Anjou-Saumur.title: Anjou and Saumur
France ~ Loire ~ White ~ Anjou-Saumur.line: Dry Chenin Blanc, much of it Savennières, plus Clos Rougeard's rare Brézé. Firm, honeyed and mineral whites for rich fish and poultry; Nicolas Joly's wines may want air, so check with the sommelier.

France ~ Loire ~ White ~ Vouvray & Toura.title: Vouvray and Touraine
France ~ Loire ~ White ~ Vouvray & Toura.line: Chenin Blanc from dry (Sec) to gently sweet (Demi-Sec) to sweet (Moelleux), led by Domaine Huet, plus crisp Jasnières. Always confirm the style on the label before you pour; the sweeter ones love spice.

France ~ Loire ~ White ~ Menetou-Salon.title: Menetou-Salon
France ~ Loire ~ White ~ Menetou-Salon.line: A neighbour of Sancerre making similar crisp Sauvignon Blanc at a gentler price. One bottle, from Henri Bourgeois.

France ~ Loire ~ White ~ Montlouis-sur-L.title: Montlouis
France ~ Loire ~ White ~ Montlouis-sur-L.line: Across the river from Vouvray, Montlouis makes Chenin Blanc from dry to sweet. One bottle, from François Chidaine; ask the sommelier how dry it is.

France ~ Loire ~ White ~ Pouilly-Fumé &.title: Sancerre and Pouilly-Fumé
France ~ Loire ~ White ~ Pouilly-Fumé &.line: The home of crisp Sauvignon Blanc, here at its most serious: Dagueneau, Cotat, Vatan and Vacheron, from $65 to rare bottles. For a guest who orders Sancerre, ask the budget and offer one classic and one splurge.

France ~ Burgundy ~ White.title: White Burgundy
France ~ Burgundy ~ White.line: The heart of the list: Chardonnay from Chablis to the Mâconnais, nearly 400 bottles from about $45 to five figures. Ask crisp and stony (Chablis) or rich and nutty (Meursault, Puligny, Chassagne), then the budget.

France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Bourgogne.title: Bourgogne
France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Bourgogne.line: Regional white Burgundy and Aligoté from great growers, Leflaive, Roulot, Coche-Dury and others, often the best value way into a famous name. Most are under $150; some, like Coche-Dury, are collector's bottles.

France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Chablis Gran.title: Chablis grand cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Chablis Gran.line: The seven grand crus on one hill above Chablis: Les Clos, Valmur, Vaudésir, Preuses, Bougros, Grenouilles, Blanchot. Rich yet stony, $195 and up. Raveneau and Dauvissat are the rarest; ask the budget.

France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Chablis Prem.title: Chablis premier cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Chablis Prem.line: Crisp, mineral Chardonnay from named slopes such as Montée de Tonnerre, Vaillons and Montmains. The sweet spot for oysters and fish; most sit between $100 and $250.

France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Chablis.title: Chablis
France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Chablis.line: Village Chablis and Petit Chablis: lean, lemony, stony Chardonnay with little or no oak, $80 to $300. A sure choice for raw oysters and a guest who dislikes buttery whites.

France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Morey-Saint-.title: Morey-Saint-Denis premier cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Morey-Saint-.line: Rare whites from red wine country: Monts Luisants from Dujac and Ponsot, whose bottling is old-vine Aligoté. Collector's bottles, around $400.

France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Vougeot Prem.title: Vougeot premier cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Vougeot Prem.line: Le Clos Blanc de Vougeot from Domaine de la Vougeraie, a rare white in red country, offered only in large bottles. A showpiece for a big table.

France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Pernand-Verg.title: Pernand-Vergelesses premier cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Pernand-Verg.line: Sous Frétille, a fine, crisp white premier cru beside the hill of Corton, from Deux Montille and Dugat-Py. Good value for the quality.

France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Pernand-Verg.title: Pernand-Vergelesses
France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Pernand-Verg.line: Village whites from beside the hill of Corton, fresh and mineral, $65 to $110. Among the best values in white Burgundy.

France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Corton-Charl.title: Corton-Charlemagne
France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Corton-Charl.line: The great white grand cru on the hill of Corton: powerful, mineral and long-lived. From Bouchard and Tollot-Beaut to Coche-Dury and Domaine de la Romanée-Conti, $550 to $5,500. Involve the sommelier.

France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Beaune Premi.title: Beaune premier cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Beaune Premi.line: White Beaune premier crus, including Jadot's Grèves Le Clos Blanc: round, ripe Chardonnay at fair prices, $105 to $230.

France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Beaune.title: Beaune
France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Beaune.line: One white village Beaune from Domaine de la Vougeraie: round and approachable.

France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Saint-Romain.title: Saint-Romain
France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Saint-Romain.line: Crisp whites from a cool, high village behind Meursault, around $110. Good value for a guest who likes Meursault but not its price.

France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Meursault Pr.title: Meursault premier cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Meursault Pr.line: Charmes, Genevrières, Perrières, Poruzots, Santenots: rich, nutty, creamy Chardonnay with depth, mostly $160 to $500 and beyond. Ideal with butter sauces and richer fish.

France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Meursault.title: Meursault
France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Meursault.line: Village Meursault, often from named sites like Les Tillets or Les Luchets: rich and nutty. Prices run from $115 to collector levels for Coche-Dury and Roulot, so ask the budget first.

France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Saint-Aubin.title: Saint-Aubin premier cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Saint-Aubin.line: Crisp, mineral whites from the slopes behind Puligny and Chassagne, $135 to $400. The value secret of white Burgundy; Hubert Lamy is the star.

France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Saint-Aubin.title: Saint-Aubin
France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Saint-Aubin.line: Village Saint-Aubin, mostly Hubert Lamy and Marc Colin: precise, mineral Chardonnay.

France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Puligny-Mont.title: Puligny-Montrachet premier cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Puligny-Mont.line: Floral, precise, elegant Chardonnay: Pucelles, Folatières, Combettes, Clavoillon, Referts. Leflaive, Sauzet and Carillon lead, mostly $200 to $600. For the guest who wants classic, refined white Burgundy.

France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Puligny-Mont.title: Puligny-Montrachet
France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Puligny-Mont.line: Village Puligny: fine and floral, $230 to $665. A strong sweet spot pick for fish and seafood.

France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Montrachet G.title: Le Montrachet
France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Montrachet G.line: The most famous white vineyard in the world, from Domaine de la Romanée-Conti, Ponsot, Sauzet and Jadot, $1,050 to $11,500. Always bring in the sommelier.

France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Chevalier-Mo.title: Chevalier-Montrachet
France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Chevalier-Mo.line: The grand cru just above Le Montrachet: tense, mineral and long, from Leflaive, Jadot's Les Demoiselles and Niellon. A celebration white.

France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Bâtard-Montr.title: Bâtard-Montrachet
France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Bâtard-Montr.line: The grand cru below Le Montrachet: rich, broad and powerful Chardonnay, $460 to $2,900. For the grandest seafood and butter sauces.

France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Bienvenue-Bâ.title: Bienvenues-Bâtard-Montrachet
France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Bienvenue-Bâ.line: A small grand cru beside Bâtard, a touch more delicate. From Leflaive, Faiveley and Paul Pernot.

France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Chassagne-Mo.title: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Chassagne-Mo.line: Rich, nutty and round: Caillerets, Morgeot, Clos Saint-Jean, La Maltroie, Les Champs Gain, mostly $150 to $500. Great with crab, shrimp and cream sauces.

France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Chassagne-Mo.title: Chassagne-Montrachet
France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Chassagne-Mo.line: Village Chassagne: rich and nutty, $160 to $350, a good sweet spot pick for richer dishes.

France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Other Côte d.title: Other Côte d'Or whites
France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Other Côte d.line: Whites from less famous villages, Ladoix, Auxey-Duresses, Savigny, Santenay, the Hautes Côtes, often from famous estates. Mostly under $150: the best value white Burgundy on the list.

France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Côte Chalonn.title: Côte Chalonnaise
France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Côte Chalonn.line: Rully, Mercurey, Givry, Montagny and Bouzeron, just south of the Côte d'Or: crisp, fresh whites around $100. A sure value pick.

France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Mâconnais.title: Mâconnais
France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Mâconnais.line: Southern Burgundy: Mâcon and Pouilly-Fuissé, riper and rounder Chardonnay, $80 to $325. Leflaive's and Lafon's Mâcons are great value doors into famous names.

France ~ Alsace ~ White.title: Alsace whites
France ~ Alsace ~ White.line: Riesling, Pinot Gris, Gewürztraminer and more from Trimbach, Weinbach, Boxler and Zind-Humbrecht. Aromatic and food-friendly with spice, $50 to $985. Ask how dry the guest likes it; some carry sweetness.

France ~ Alsace ~ White ~ Gewürztraminer.title: Gewürztraminer
France ~ Alsace ~ White ~ Gewürztraminer.line: Exotic, rose and lychee-scented whites, often off-dry, some late harvest. Beautiful with spice and rich dishes; confirm sweetness before pouring.

France ~ Alsace ~ White ~ Pinot Gris.title: Pinot Gris
France ~ Alsace ~ White ~ Pinot Gris.line: Rich, smoky, textured Alsace whites, sometimes with sweetness. Good with pork, poultry and spiced Creole flavours.

France ~ Alsace ~ White ~ Riesling.title: Alsace Riesling
France ~ Alsace ~ White ~ Riesling.line: Mostly dry, firm, mineral Riesling, from Trimbach's Clos Ste Hune to Boxler's grand crus. Ideal for a guest who wants Riesling without sweetness.

France ~ Alsace ~ White ~ Sylvaner.title: Sylvaner
France ~ Alsace ~ White ~ Sylvaner.line: Light, fresh, gently herbal Alsace whites, $55 to $75. Easy value bottles.

France ~ Alsace ~ White ~ Other Varietie.title: Other Alsace whites
France ~ Alsace ~ White ~ Other Varietie.line: Muscat, Pinot Blanc, Edelzwicker blends and Marcel Deiss's field blends: aromatic and easygoing, mostly under $150.

France ~ Rhône~ White.title: Rhône whites
France ~ Rhône~ White.line: Viognier from Condrieu, Marsanne from Hermitage and round southern blends, $80 to $550. Rich, textured whites for crab, shrimp and spiced dishes; ask whether the guest wants floral or nutty.

France ~ Rhône~ White ~ Condrieu.title: Condrieu
France ~ Rhône~ White ~ Condrieu.line: Viognier at its finest: apricot, flowers and a silky texture, $145 to $250. Wonderful with crab and gentle spice.

France ~ Rhône~ White ~ Hermitage.title: White Hermitage
France ~ Rhône~ White ~ Hermitage.line: Marsanne-led, rich, honeyed and long-lived, from Chave, Jaboulet, Guigal and others. A grand white for rich fish and veal.

France ~ Rhône~ White ~ Châteauneuf-duPa.title: White Châteauneuf-du-Pape
France ~ Rhône~ White ~ Châteauneuf-duPa.line: Round, floral southern whites, a rare style. Two bottles.

France ~ Rhône~ White ~ Other Rhône.title: Other Rhône whites
France ~ Rhône~ White ~ Other Rhône.line: Crozes-Hermitage, Saint-Péray, Côtes du Rhône and southern villages, many from great red wine estates. Round, aromatic and good value, mostly under $150.

France ~ Other ~ White.title: Other French whites
France ~ Other ~ White.line: Bordeaux, the Jura, Provence, Jurançon and the Languedoc, from $55 to Haut-Brion. Ask what the guest likes; this corner rewards curiosity.

France ~ Other ~ White ~ Bordeaux.title: White Bordeaux
France ~ Other ~ White ~ Bordeaux.line: Sauvignon Blanc and Sémillon from Pessac-Léognan and beyond: crisp, citrusy, lightly oaked. From $60 to Haut-Brion at $2,500; great with seafood.

France ~ Other ~ White ~ Jurançon.title: Jurançon
France ~ Other ~ White ~ Jurançon.line: One dry white from the foothills of the Pyrenees, crisp and exotic.

France ~ Other ~ White ~ Savoie & Jura.title: Jura
France ~ Other ~ White ~ Savoie & Jura.line: Chardonnay and Savagnin from the Jura, including Vin Jaune, aged under a veil of yeast, nutty and intense. Distinctive and savoury; check the guest wants something unusual.

France ~ Other ~ White ~ Provence.title: Provence whites
France ~ Other ~ White ~ Provence.line: Château Simone, Tempier, Trévallon and the Luberon: herbal, round whites. Ask whether the guest wants rare or easygoing.

France ~ Other ~ White ~ Languedoc-Rouss.title: Languedoc whites
France ~ Other ~ White ~ Languedoc-Rouss.line: Grange des Pères, a cult white, and a Limoux Chenin Blanc: from value to rare.

Austria & Hungary.title: Austria and Hungary
Austria & Hungary.line: Grüner Veltliner and dry Riesling from the Wachau, Kamptal and Kremstal, plus Tokaj Furmint, $50 to $690. Crisp, peppery and mineral; ideal with seafood and vegetables.

Austria & Hungary ~ Kamptal.title: Kamptal
Austria & Hungary ~ Kamptal.line: Bründlmayer, Hirsch, Loimer and Schloss Gobelsburg: dry Riesling from the Heiligenstein and peppery Grüner Veltliner. From easy half-bottles to rare magnums.

Austria & Hungary ~ Kremstal.title: Kremstal
Austria & Hungary ~ Kremstal.line: Grüner Veltliner from around the town of Krems, mostly crisp, peppery and good value.

Austria & Hungary ~ Wachau.title: Wachau
Austria & Hungary ~ Wachau.line: Austria's most famous whites, steep Danube terraces. Federspiel is the lighter dry style, Smaragd the ripest; all dry. Great with rich fish.

Austria & Hungary ~ Burgenland.title: Burgenland
Austria & Hungary ~ Burgenland.line: One bottle from Gut Oggau, a biodynamic estate: a textured Grüner Veltliner blend.

Austria & Hungary ~ Hungary.title: Hungary
Austria & Hungary ~ Hungary.line: One dry Furmint from Tokaj, crisp and smoky, $75.

Germany ~ White.title: German whites
Germany ~ White.line: Mostly Riesling from the Mosel, Rheingau, Rheinhessen, Nahe and Pfalz, $45 to $950. Ask dry or a touch sweet: Trocken and GG are dry, Kabinett, Spätlese and Auslese are usually sweeter.

Germany ~ White ~ Riesling.title: German Riesling
Germany ~ White ~ Riesling.line: From light, gently sweet Kabinett to dry grand cru GG. Read the label words with the guest and match sweetness to spice: off-dry Riesling loves Creole heat.

Germany ~ White ~ Riesling ~ Mosel.title: Mosel
Germany ~ White ~ Riesling ~ Mosel.line: Light, delicate, slate-grown Riesling, often low in alcohol, from Egon Müller, JJ Prüm and Peter Lauer. Many are gently sweet; Trocken means dry.

Germany ~ White ~ Riesling ~ Rheingau.title: Rheingau
Germany ~ White ~ Riesling ~ Rheingau.line: Fuller, firm Riesling from J.B. Becker, Robert Weil and Georg Breuer, much of it dry. Becker's wines are released with age.

Germany ~ White ~ Riesling ~ Rheinhessen.title: Rheinhessen
Germany ~ White ~ Riesling ~ Rheinhessen.line: Keller and Gunderloch: powerful dry grand crus and a few gently sweet Kabinetts. Keller's GGs are among the most sought-after whites in Germany.

Germany ~ White ~ Riesling ~ Nahe.title: Nahe
Germany ~ White ~ Riesling ~ Nahe.line: Dönnhoff, Emrich-Schönleber, Diel, Hexamer and Kruger-Rumpf: Riesling between Mosel delicacy and Pfalz power, dry and sweet.

Germany ~ White ~ Riesling ~ Pfalz.title: Pfalz
Germany ~ White ~ Riesling ~ Pfalz.line: Warmer and fuller, mostly dry Riesling from Bürklin-Wolf, Von Winning and von Buhl. Good with richer dishes.

Germany ~ White ~ Other.title: Other German whites
Germany ~ White ~ Other.line: Chardonnay, Pinot Blanc, Sauvignon Blanc and Silvaner from Rheinhessen, the Pfalz and Franken, mostly under $110.

Germany ~ White ~ Other ~ Rheinhessen.title: Other Rheinhessen whites
Germany ~ White ~ Other ~ Rheinhessen.line: Two Chardonnay-based whites from Moritz Kissinger and Knewitz: fresh and fine.

Germany ~ White ~ Other ~ Franken.title: Franken
Germany ~ White ~ Other ~ Franken.line: One dry Silvaner from Hans Wirsching, earthy and good value.

Germany ~ White ~ Other ~ Pfalz.title: Other Pfalz whites
Germany ~ White ~ Other ~ Pfalz.line: One Sauvignon Blanc from Von Winning.

Italy & Greece ~ White.title: Italian and Greek whites
Italy & Greece ~ White.line: From Alto Adige to Santorini: crisp, saline, textured whites, mostly under $175. Ask whether the guest wants fresh and crisp or textured and characterful.

Italy & Greece ~ White ~ Greece.title: Greece
Italy & Greece ~ White ~ Greece.line: One Assyrtiko from Santorini, crisp and saline, great with seafood.

Italy & Greece ~ White ~ Italy.title: Italy
Italy & Greece ~ White ~ Italy.line: Whites from the Alps to Campania and Liguria: Terlano, Friulano, Petite Arvine, Falanghina, Vitovska. Mostly crisp; some are textured.

Spain ~ White.title: Spanish whites
Spain ~ White.line: Albariño from Rías Baixas, Godello from Bierzo, Canary Island Listán Blanco and aged white Rioja, $65 to $195. Crisp, saline and food-friendly; López de Heredia is the outlier, aged and nutty.

United States ~ Chardonnay.title: American Chardonnay
United States ~ Chardonnay.line: California, Oregon and Washington Chardonnay, $30 to $950, from lean and mineral to rich and creamy. Ask buttery or crisp first, then point to Napa for richness, the coast for freshness.

United States ~ Chardonnay ~ California.title: California Chardonnay
United States ~ Chardonnay ~ California.line: Napa, Sonoma and the Central Coast: from classic rich and creamy to lean, modern styles.

United States ~ Chardonnay ~ California.title: Sonoma Chardonnay
United States ~ Chardonnay ~ California.line: Cooler, often brighter Chardonnay from the Sonoma Coast and Russian River: Kistler, Ramey, Hirsch, Lioco. Good with fish and crab.

United States ~ Chardonnay ~ California.title: Napa Chardonnay
United States ~ Chardonnay ~ California.line: Classic Napa: Montelena, Cakebread, Far Niente, Kongsgaard and the lean mountain wines of Mayacamas and Stony Hill. Ask rich or restrained.

United States ~ Chardonnay ~ California.title: Central Coast Chardonnay
United States ~ Chardonnay ~ California.line: Santa Barbara, Monterey and Mount Harlan: cool-climate, often lean and mineral Chardonnay, mostly under $150. Great value.

United States ~ Chardonnay ~ Oregon & Wa.title: Oregon and Washington Chardonnay
United States ~ Chardonnay ~ Oregon & Wa.line: Fresh, taut Chardonnay from Willamette Valley, plus library bottles from Eyrie. A strong pick for a Burgundy lover.

United States ~ Sauvignon Blanc.title: American Sauvignon Blanc
United States ~ Sauvignon Blanc.line: Crisp, citrusy California and Oregon Sauvignon Blanc, mostly under $100. Easy, fresh picks for salads, fish and lighter dishes.

United States ~ Sauvignon Blanc ~ Califo.title: California Sauvignon Blanc
United States ~ Sauvignon Blanc ~ Califo.line: From Duckhorn and Mondavi to the richer, textured Arkenstone and Jonata Flor, $35 to $270.

United States ~ Sauvignon Blanc ~ Oregon.title: Oregon Sauvignon Blanc
United States ~ Sauvignon Blanc ~ Oregon.line: One bottle from Patricia Green, crisp and fresh.

United States ~ Other ~ White.title: Other American whites
United States ~ Other ~ White.line: Viognier, Riesling, Ribolla, Picpoul and blends from California, Oregon and New York, $45 to $320. For a guest who wants something different from Chardonnay.

United States ~ Other ~ White ~ Unique W.title: Unique American whites
United States ~ Other ~ White ~ Unique W.line: Unusual grapes and blends: Au Bon Climat's Hildegard, Matthiasson's Ribolla Gialla, Finger Lakes Riesling and more. Ask what the guest likes and suggest a discovery.

International ~ White.title: Whites from the southern hemisphere
International ~ White.line: Argentina, Australia, Chile, New Zealand and South Africa: Chardonnay, Chenin Blanc, Riesling and Semillon, $50 to $560. Ask whether the guest wants classic Chardonnay or something new.

International ~ White ~ Argentina.title: Argentina
International ~ White ~ Argentina.line: High-altitude and Patagonian Chardonnay from Catena Zapata, Chacra and El Enemigo.

International ~ White ~ Australia.title: Australia
International ~ White ~ Australia.line: Chardonnay from Victoria, Riesling from Clare and Tasmania, Hunter Semillon. Giaconda is a rare collector's bottle.

International ~ White ~ Chile.title: Chile
International ~ White ~ Chile.line: One Chardonnay from the Atacama desert, crisp and saline.

International ~ White ~ New Zealand.title: New Zealand
International ~ White ~ New Zealand.line: Chardonnay from Kumeu River near Auckland, fine and taut, $50 to $155.

International ~ White ~ South Africa.title: South Africa
International ~ White ~ South Africa.line: Old-vine Chenin Blanc and white blends from Swartland and Stellenbosch, led by Sadie. Textured, characterful whites with great value at the lower end.

Rosé.title: Rosé
Rosé.line: Fifteen bottles, mostly dry Provence and Sancerre rosé, plus Bandol and Pascal Cotat for depth, $45 to $270. Ask light and crisp or something with more body for food.

Rosé ~ France.title: French rosé
Rosé ~ France.line: Pale, dry Provence rosé, Whispering Angel and friends, then Tempier's Bandol and Sancerre from Crochet and Cotat for food. Magnums suit a table.

Rosé ~ Italy.title: Italian rosé
Rosé ~ Italy.line: One Ligurian rosé from the Ciliegiolo grape, fresh and fruity.

Rosé ~ United States.title: American rosé
